data.report:
## Heeler iOS app internals (github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler, Apache-2.0, Swift 6)
Sources: AGENTS.md (→CLAUDE.md), CONTEXT.md (336 lines), PRIVACY.md, plugin/README.md (546 lines), docs/adr/0001-0016, docs/guides/vps-jump-host.md, docs/agents/live-activity-contract.md, relay/README, CHANGELOG.md. Evidence paths are repo-relative; [INFERENCE] marks claims not stated verbatim.

### 1. Transport (ADR-0002 superseded by ADR-0011; README 'How it connects')
- History: v1 used exec + socat (ADR-0002): per-request `socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<sock>` exec channels + one long-lived channel for `events.subscribe`; `exec herdr agent attach <pane>` bootstrap line in a PTY shell. Required socat on every host.
- Current (ADR-0011 accepted): repository-local `Packages/HeelerSSH` wrapping libssh2 + OpenSSL (checked-in XCFrameworks). Each herdr request opens a `direct-streamlocal` channel onto the herdr Unix socket (`herdr.sock`); one long-lived reserved channel carries the event stream; interactive terminals run `herdr agent attach --takeover` on an SSH PTY. Direct connections use non-blocking POSIX sockets (DispatchSourceRead/Write); nested Jump Host sessions use an internal byte transport over an outer `direct-tcpip` channel. Every SSH hop has one non-blocking session driver that serializes all `LIBSSH2_SESSION` calls.
- herdr JSON API is NDJSON over a Unix domain socket, ONE REQUEST PER CONNECTION, so each RPC opens its own direct-streamlocal channel (bounded by forwarding-budget queue, 8 ordinary RPC + 1 reserved events; 8 exec/SFTP + 1 reserved Attach in the session budget). `agent.prompt` (no `wait`) returns immediately as delivery acknowledgment; `wait` variant was rejected (occupies an RPC channel for an agent turn).
- Events stream: `events.subscribe` on a dedicated channel — real-time while foregrounded; herdr replays NO state on subscribe (ADR-0011/0012), so Agent Inventory is replaced wholesale on each snapshot. `pane.agent_status_changed` is the precise, tiny, usable push signal; `pane_output_changed` isn't subscribable and `pane.output_matched` is edge-triggered (ADR-0012) — rejected as a refresh signal. herdr `ping` is the authoritative health check (exercises SSH, both jumps, streamlocal, socket, server).
- Takeover/PTY: `herdr agent attach` resolves an Agent over the API to its terminal_id and calls `run_terminal_attach` (per herdr v0.8.2 source, ADR-0015). `terminal attach` targets a terminal ID via the client socket (`herdr.sock`→`herdr-client.sock`, server/socket_paths.rs); supports raw input, resize, and `--takeover`. One writable attach owner per terminal; a second attach without --takeover is refused; takeover displaces the prior owner with an explicit shutdown message. Missing terminal fails outright (no hang). Unix-only.
- Stream-local failure classification: libssh2 can't distinguish stale socket vs forwarding-policy denial; Heeler runs one read-only remote `test -S` diagnostic. Socket missing → socketNotFound; socket exists → one honest combined 'herdr not running OR streamlocal disabled' failure, deliberately NOT retryable (user must fix).
- Attach Link: web URLs observed in terminal during a detail session are collected and remain available until leaving detail (CONTEXT.md; ADR-0010).

### 2. Console data model (ADR-0012/0013; plugin sidebar snapshot v1; CONTEXT.md)
- Agents across Hosts rendered as a flat list or by-Host grouped list with collapsible sections, sorted Blocked-first, filterable by Host, searchable. Per-agent model (`AgentInfo`/`ConsoleAgent`, files under Sources/Heeler/Console/: AgentCardView, AgentRowLayout, AgentArgumentsField, AgentName).
- herdr JSON fields driving the agent list: `pane_id`, `workspace_id`, `agent` (kind: claude/codex/...), `display_agent`/`name`, `agent_status` (idle/working/blocked/done/unknown), `terminal_id`, `cwd`, `terminal_title`/`terminal_title_stripped`, `state_icon`/`state_text` (sidebar tokens), `rows_by_agent` per-kind layout overrides, workspace label via `workspace list`. Agent Status (Blocked) drives sort order + notifications. State icon appears as the Row-1 status badge, never a field.
- Agent Row Layout: 3 fixed Row Slots per Host; Rows 1-2 come from the Host's herdr sidebar layout (plugin snapshot `sidebar.json`, ADR plugin 0.4.0), Row 3 is Heeler's. herdr per-kind `rows_by_agent` overrides are decoded but not applied. Order: user-saved layout > plugin snapshot > Heeler default; never merged. Sync-from-plugin refills Rows 1-2.
- 'New Agent' can start in an existing Workspace, a new Worktree of one, or a new Workspace at a remote directory; uses `tab.create` (workspace_id + concrete cwd + focus:false, ADR-0015) and create-agent APIs. There IS an Agent switcher (shared by detail surfaces) at the bottom of the Composer — so yes, there is pane/agent switching UI; workspaces/worktrees are launch targets, not a browse-list surface. Agent Inventory readiness modeled separately (unknown vs loading vs empty).

### 3. Composer internals (ADR-0012 superseded by ADR-0013; ADR-0009, 0016)
- Composer is the DEFAULT authored input on Agent detail: a native draft field that composes fully on-device (iOS keyboard with autocorrect/IME/dictation) and delivers in ONE piece via one `agent.prompt` request (without `wait`) — no remote-echo latency while drafting, no keystroke round-trips. When Agent Status is Blocked, Send inserts the draft into the Attach PTY without Enter (herdr 0.8.2 rejects `agent.prompt` while blocked because auto-Enter would confirm/dismiss a dialog); the tools keyboard submits (Enter) or cancels (Esc).
- Direct Input (ADR-0016): opt-in app-wide preference, default off; hides Composer, routes the iOS keyboard + a compact app-owned shortcut row (Esc/Tab/Shift-Tab/Enter) into the live Attach PTY; Skills/Snippets still insert into the draft/pane without Enter.
- Tools keyboard: tabbed pad with large Agent controls (Esc/Tab/Shift-Tab/arrows/Enter/Backspace → directly to PTY) and a full Terminal keyboard (characters, Ctrl/Alt/Shift, fn keys) via libghostty `UITerminalView.sendKey`; Skills and Snippets panels only insert text into the draft (ADR-0009 insert-without-submit).
- Skills (Sources/Heeler/Skills/) and Snippets (Snippets/) insert into the Composer draft and nothing more; the user still delivers. Skills are herdr agent skills surfaced in the tools pad; Snippets are a global user set, optional Title, multiline wrapped in bracketed paste (`ESC[200~...ESC[201~`) when the app tracked DECSET 2004.
- Attachments (ADR-0006): Add stages one image (decoded/bounded/metadata-stripped) or file (≤64 MiB, random local name, safe extension kept) over SFTP to private Host temp dirs (atomic completion); the resulting Host path is copied to an expiring local clipboard (24h) and appended to the draft with a trailing space — never auto-submitted. Completed Host files outlive the screen (ADR-0005).
- libghostty (ADR-0004): `InMemoryTerminalSession` — PTY bytes in via `receive(_:)`, Ghostty write/resize callbacks feed Attach transport. Heeler owns two-mode keyboard, touch-scroll routing (normal-buffer → scrollback actions; alternate-screen → SGR/legacy wheel encoding via a tracked DEC private-mode tracker), native text-selection sheet, URL policy, and pinch zoom (Ghostty's own pinch disabled; app routes through TerminalController persisted size). Ghostty's fixterms encoding preserves Ctrl-I/Tab vs Ctrl-M/Enter distinctions.

### 4. E2E-encrypted push + Live Activities (ADR-0008, ADR-0014, PRIVACY.md, plugin README, live-activity-contract.md)
- Pipeline: herdr plugin `[[events]]` hooks on `pane.agent_status_changed` run short-lived Node scripts (notify-hook.js for alerts; activity-hook.js for Live Activity). Notify hook debounces (~5s, re-checks status via `herdr agent get <pane>`), dedupes, and for eligible devices POSTs to the relay. herdr runs BOTH hooks per event (verified 0.8.0).
- Push Relay (https://heeler-apns.bybee.dev, Cloudflare Workers, stateless): holds the APNs `.p8`, signs ES256 JWT, forwards to Apple. No accounts/db/queues/durable storage; device tokens + ciphertext + source IP + timing pass through in volatile per-instance memory with 1-minute rate limits. Cannot read content (never receives the Notification Key). Custom relay URL supported for self-built apps; must use APNs creds for that bundle ID.
- End-to-end encryption: per-Host symmetric Notification Key generated on device, stored in shared Keychain (AfterFirstUnlock; mirrored in shared container protected-until-first-unlock, backup-excluded), copied to the Host in `notifications.json` (plugin config dir via `herdr plugin config-dir`). Envelope `{v:1, kid, n, ct}` — AES-256-GCM, 12-byte nonce, AAD `HERDR-NOTIFY:1`, kid = first 8 bytes of SHA-256(key). App's Notification Service Extension decrypts; untrusted/corrupt → generic fallback banner.
- Notification Registration: app writes push token + Notification Key over SSH; per host, repeatable, independent of pairing. Devices fan out edge-side (one entry per token). `410 Unregistered` → plugin prunes dead token.
- Triggers: Blocked + Done (Done individually toggleable; Working/Idle never alert). Foreground: system push banners silenced, in-app banner driven off the app's own live event stream (near-zero latency, mirrors plugin gates).
- Live Activities (ADR-0014): one per Host. App starts locally (`pushType:.token`) and writes per-activity token + `pinned_pane_ids` + resolved `row_layout` + `host_name` into registration file; after suspension the plugin activity-hook lists agents (`herdr agent list`), resolves workspace labels, coalesces (1.5s latest-wins claim + unchanged suppression), and posts update/end. HYBRID content-state: plaintext counts {working,blocked,done} + encrypted details envelope (AAD `HERDR-ACTIVITY:1`, agents[] with kind/name/pane/status/title/workspace/rows, capped at 5 visible) decrypted at render time by the widget from shared Keychain. Counts + update/end/priority/timestamp are cleartext to the relay (relayed to APNs) because Live Activity pushes have no service-extension hook and the system must decode content-state; per-agent identity stays encrypted. Statuses: working/blocked/done shown, idle/unknown hidden. Priority 5 default, 10 only for a newly-blocked agent. No push-to-start in v1 (killed app ~50% success; new working agent while app dead isn't seen until next run). AgentActivityAttributes name is shipped forever (APNs attributes-type). Live Activity shows counts + pinned rows; Dynamic Island compact = counts.

### 5. QR pairing (ADR-0007; plugin README)
- `herdr plugin install ZingerLittleBee/Heeler/plugin --ref main --yes`, then `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` renders a QR in a herdr popup pane. Envelope: `HERDR-PAIR:<version>:<base64url(JSON)>`.
- Payload v1: `addrs` (candidate addresses in try order), `port` (fixed at 22 currently — known limitation), `user`, `fp` (host key fingerprint `SHA256:`+43 unpadded base64, pinned instead of TOFU), optional `seed` (raw 32-byte Bootstrap Key Ed25519 seed) + `exp` (Unix-seconds TTL). No seed/exp = config-only code. Decoders ignore unknown fields; canonical encoding asserted by shared test vectors.
- Bootstrap Key lifecycle: ephemeral Ed25519 generated on the Host, single-use, 2-minute TTL; public half written to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` as a restricted line `restrict,command="'<node>' '<plugin>/src/pair-accept.js' ... --pairing-id <id>"` with comment `herdr-pairing:<id>:exp:<unix>`. The forced command performs Enrollment only. Removed on success (self-revoke), TTL expiry, popup exit, or a sweep of expired lines at next start. Pending state in `$HERDR_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR/pending/`, never the checkout.
- Enrollment: app connects with Bootstrap Key (raw seed), writes its Device Key public line + newline to stdin; server answers `HERDR-ENROLL:OK:<SHA256:fp>` (appended/authored, bootstrap revoked, exit 0) or typed ERR lines (invalid_key, no_input, expired, unknown_pairing). Then app reconnects with the Device Key. Host persisted only after the full ceremony.
- App: Device Key = Ed25519 keypair generated on-device, private half stays in Keychain; public half is what a Host authorizes. Pairing uses a dedicated one-shot client beside Transport. Fallbacks: manual Host form + copy-paste authorized_keys line. Risk accepted: same-room attacker photographing the QR and racing within TTL. Reachability scoped to same-LAN/same-VPN; cellular-only phones unsupported.

### 6. libghostty terminal + takeover + SFTP attachments
- libghostty-spm (ADR-0004): UIKit `UITerminalView` + `InMemoryTerminalSession`; owns parsing, Metal rendering, CoreText, IME, scrollback. Heeler owns keyboards, touch-scroll routing, selection sheet, URL policy, Attach lifecycle. Pinched version; verify SwiftPM checksum before updates. Uses `sendKey` API (libghostty-spm ≥1.6.20260909). ~30 themes, JetBrains Mono & IBM Plex Mono bundled, pinch zoom app-owned.
- Takeover semantics (ADR-0015): Shell Terminal (Open Terminal) creates a fresh herdr tab via `tab.create` in the Agent's cwd (then worktree path), then attaches the returned root pane's shell through `herdr terminal attach <terminal_id> --takeover` on the existing SSH PTY pipeline. Takeover is safe because the tab is freshly minted; the flow never targets an arbitrary existing terminal (would displace a desktop attach owner). Back detaches, leaving the remote tab alive for desktop handoff. Agent Attach `--takeover` similarly displaces a stale terminal owner. One Host terminal lifetime: opening Shell Terminal tears Agent Attach down first; leaving lets it rejoin.
- Attachments over SFTP (ADR-0006): Transport.stageImage/stageFile share one SFTP impl (private Host tmp dirs, restrictive perms, partial-file compensation, atomic completion, shared session-channel budget). ≤64 MiB files; images re-encoded metadata-stripped. No PTY binary injection (terminal input has no file framing).

### 7. Worktrees, jump hosts, rough edges
- Worktrees (CONTEXT.md): a fresh `git checkout` of a workspace's repo created by herdr as its own workspace; branch defaults to herdr's generated `worktree/<name>` off HEAD; removing the Worktree deletes the checkout and closes its workspace but the branch survives. Snapshot worktree metadata describes the main checkout; only `is_linked_worktree` makes a workspace eligible for linked-Worktree removal. New Agent can start in a new Worktree.
- Jump Hosts (docs/guides/vps-jump-host.md + vps-jump-host-setup.md): reach unroutable Macs behind NAT via a restricted VPS. Mac makes a persistent outbound reverse-SSH tunnel (launchd) publishing a loopback-only port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:2222); iOS connects to the VPS (herdr-jump account, direct-tcpip to 127.0.0.1:2222 only, `AllowTcpForwarding local`, `PermitOpen 127.0.0.1:2222`, `MaxSessions 0`), then does a SECOND SSH handshake to the Mac. Keys verified at both hops; Device Key authorized on both the VPS jump account and the Mac. VPS can observe metadata/interrupt but not passively read the inner session while host keys are verified. No stream-local over the jump; nested driver uses outer direct-tcpip as transport.
- Rough edges / limitations (documented): requires Node ≥20 + herdr ≥0.7.5 + OpenSSH with stream-local forwarding enabled (onboarding calls out when disabled); advertised SSH port fixed at 22 (plugin README known limitation); herdr API wire shapes carry no stability guarantee (hooks parse leniently); no push-to-start for Live Activities; Live Activity widget shows counts-only on watch/pre-first-unlock; remote history NOT addressable (`pane.read` visible/recent + 1000-line cap, no offset) so no server-side scroll history; shell tabs not projected into Console and outside notification routing; Agent Attach is display-only under Composer (dual-prompt collision); relay is a single point of failure for notifications only (Console/Attach never touch it); App Store availability limited by country; personal-use emphasis 'expect rough edges'. [INFERENCE: no separate 'sync' beyond the sidebar-layout plugin export; no multi-account server.]

Two data channels: (1) host->app polling/commands over SSH exec + SFTP file transfers; (2) asynchronous notifications: drover.notify on the host POSTs 'blocked' events over HTTPS to Firebase Functions (Bearer host credential), which relays via FCM to the device; the device itself only registers an FCM token and creates pairing codes. data.report:
DROVER INTERNALS (keinstn/drover, MIT; Flutter app + Firebase Functions backend). drover-notify plugin is a separate repo (keinstn/drover-notify).

1) TRANSPORT / CLI vs SOCKET — SSH via dartssh2 (pubspec: dartssh2 ^4.1.0). It drives the herdr CLI over SSH, NOT a direct socket API (spike.dart + SshCommandRunner run `herdr <args>` in one exec each, serialized on a mutex, one channel at a time). infra/ssh_command_runner.dart: SSHSocket.connect + SSHClient, private key from PEM + optional passphrase (SSHKeyPair.fromPem), host-key trust-on-first-use with fingerprint pinning and SshHostKeyMismatchException, 10s auth + exec timeout bounds, drops a wedged client on SSHChannelOpenError/Timeout, connection invalidation on network change, mutex-serialized channel use, UTF-8 lossy decode. Host OS auto-detected (uname -s / cmd.exe ver); WindowsHostPlatform assembles PowerShell -EncodedCommand lines (forces UTF-8, exits with $LASTEXITCODE). Commands (herdr_client.dart): agent list/get/read --source recent --format ansi/prompt/start --kind --pane/rename; pane send-text/send-keys/close/split/list; workspace create --no-focus/list/close/rename; plugin list --plugin <id> --json; plugin config-dir; herdr --version. Errors parsed from JSON envelope {error:{code,message}} on BOTH channels regardless of exit code. SFTP (dartssh2 SftpClient) used for uploadFile/readFile/statFile/listDirectory/resolvePath (images and native transcript files).

2) TRANSCRIPT HISTORY + RENDERING — Two sources. (a) NATIVE via `agent_session` (present only when a herdr integration hook is installed: herdr integration install claude/codex/copilot/pi/omp; only from the NEXT SessionStart). Adapters: Claude, Copilot, Codex, Pi, Omp (agent_registry.dart). JSONL files located on host (Claude under ~/.claude/projects, found by session id) and read over SFTP via JsonlTranscriptWindow: bounded 512KiB tail window initial load, append-only polling (only bytes past known EOF), pull-to-load-more paging older chunks, truncation/replaced-file reset, oversized-record skip. Parsed to TranscriptMessage / TranscriptToolUse / TranscriptThinking / TranscriptToolResult. (b) PANE-TEXT FALLBACK for unmapped agents: `agent read --source recent --format ansi` (bounded by herdr's retained pane buffer). ansi_text.dart parses SGR escapes into styled runs; pane_text.dart stripTuiChrome() strips box-drawing rules (─), `-- INSERT --` mode lines, status/mode glyph lines, empty `❯` prompts. Turn markers per herdr-notes Measurements: `❯` user, `⏺` assistant/action, `✻ Worked for Ns` meta footer; trailing `-- INSERT --` mode line stripped. Session title from herdr `terminal_title_stripped` (drops one leading spinner glyph) + client-side suffix strip (e.g. ' - GitHub Copilot').

3) PERMISSION PROMPTS -> BUTTONS — (a) Structured-prompt capability per agent from native JSONL (Claude AskUserQuestion tool_use: input.questions[]{question,header,multiSelect,options[]}; 'pending' = last unanswered tool_use via findLastUnansweredToolUse). Answered by injecting keys through the TUI: option digits / custom text via `pane send-text`, Enter/arrows via `pane send-keys`; READ-DRIVEN injector (re-reads pane after each keystroke, aborts on unknown state; dialog detected by 'Esc to cancel' footer; multi-select: digits toggle then right -> Submit '1. Submit answers'). (b) GENERIC FALLBACK: parsePromptOptions() scans last 30 lines for numbered-option prompt via regex `^(\s*)(❯\s*)?(\d+)\.\s+(\S.*)$`, requires >=2 options numbered 1..N consecutively, marks selected (❯), derives question from preceding line ending '?'; tapping types that digit.

4) NOTIFICATIONS — Firebase backend (functions/). What leaves the DEVICE: FCM token + deviceId + platform + notifyOnBlocked/notifyOnDone, registered under Firebase Auth anonymous uid (registerDevice onCall, App Check App Attest iOS); createPairingCode(hostId) -> pairing code. The EVENT payload leaves the HOST, not the device: the drover.notify herdr plugin POSTs ONLY `blocked` to the Functions HTTP endpoint sendBlockedNotification, body {hostId, paneId, eventId(UUID), agentName?, status}, header Authorization: Bearer <host credential>. Relay: pairing code (randomBytes(32) base64url) and host credential (randomBytes(32) base64url) are stored/checked ONLY as SHA-256 hashes (pairingCode doc id = sha256; credentialHash via timingSafeEqual); completePairing exchanges a one-time 10-min code for credential + notificationUrl; sendBlockedNotification authorizes, dedupes by eventId (Firestore events collection, 24h TTL), then FCM multicast-delivers (title 'Agent needs your input' / 'Agent finished'). Device on receipt validates hostId against saved config and opens the pane on tap. E2E encryption: NO. {hostId,paneId,eventId,agentName} travel in plaintext (TLS in transit, visible to the Firebase project); only credentials/pairing codes are hashed. Schema supports 'done'/notifyOnDone but the shipped plugin only sends blocked.

5) VOICE + PHOTO — Voice: speech_to_text ^7.4.0, ON-DEVICE dictation only (ListenMode.dictation, partialResults, autoPunctuation, cancelOnError, onDevice:true; ja_JP for ja); capability probed via platform channel com.keinstn.drover/speech 'supportsOnDeviceRecognition'; one shared SpeechInputController (plugin singleton). Photo: image_picker ^1.2.3 (gallery single/multi; camera iOS-only); read bytes + sanitized extension ([a-z0-9], fallback png); uploaded via SFTP to `<cwd>/.drover/img-<ts>-<i>.<ext>`, writes .gitignore '*', prunes img-* >2 days; referenced from an ordinary text prompt as a bare absolute path (Claude) or @mention (Copilot) — agent-specific; staying under cwd avoids out-of-workspace read permission prompts.

6) LIMITATIONS / ROUGH EDGES — herdr version floor 0.8.0 enforced per host (persistent warning + blocks launches below; agent prompt/start --pane/wait --until require it); herdr-api-snapshot unreleased (uses agent list); integration must be installed BEFORE SessionStart or native history silently falls back to pane-text (bounded buffer; install doesn't affect running agents); a send right after agent start can be silently dropped (confirm by re-polling); agent start without explicit --workspace hijacks the focused workspace (closing it kills the agent); mode cycling needs raw-backtab workaround ESC[Z via pane send-text (pane send-keys shift+tab broken up to herdr 0.8.0/0.8.2 — writes a plain Tab byte, fails silently); input channel is text-only, no synthetic image paste (SFTP+path); herdr plugin install clones over unauthenticated HTTPS (can't fetch private repos; use git clone + herdr plugin link); error envelope channel/exit code inconsistent (must probe both stdout+stderr); agent `name` is a slug not a display title (uses terminal_title_stripped); Windows admin hosts need public key in C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys; pairing config.json holds the host credential (don't copy/commit); notifications only on blocked (no done in practice); App Check only on iOS Release; on-device speech required (no network STT); free Apple ID signing expires after 7 days.

HOST REQUIREMENTS — SSH with key-based auth; herdr >=0.8.0; one herdr integration per agent for native transcripts; Node >=18 for the drover.notify plugin (zero npm deps).

Focusing on **Heeler vs Whip** — the two most mature by internals — with Drover as the reference point you already run:

## Transport: how each talks to herdr

| | **Heeler** (Swift, 324★) | **Whip** (Rust core + React Native, 66★) | Drover (for contrast) |
|---|---|---|---|
| SSH library | libssh2 via repo-local XCFramework (deliberately switched away from Citadel/swift-nio-ssh — ADR-0011) | russh, wrapped in a shared **Rust core** (`whip-ssh` + one TurboModule) | dartssh2 |
| herdr surface | **Direct socket API**: every RPC opens a `direct-streamlocal` channel onto `herdr.sock`; NDJSON; one-request-per-connection, with an 8+1 channel budget under OpenSSH's default `MaxSessions 10` | **Direct socket API**: same stream-local channels — short-lived request channels + one persistent `events.subscribe` channel (JSONL, replay-in-flight) + per-pane **client-protocol socket** for terminals with binary length-prefixed ANSI frames (no JSON on the hot path) | **herdr CLI over SSH exec** — runs `herdr agent list` etc. as commands, parses JSON envelopes. No socket API at all |
| Terminal rendering | libghostty (Metal, real emulator) + `herdr agent attach --takeover` on an SSH PTY | xterm.js in a WebView, fed binary ANSI from the Rust core | none (chat-only) |
| Protocol versioning | herdr API "no wire stability guarantee" — parses leniently | explicit ping→pong handshake, accepts herdr protocols **17–22**, versioned projections | version floor check, CLI JSON envelope parsing |

The architectural split: **Heeler and Whip both speak herdr's native Unix-socket protocol over SSH stream-local channels** — structured, event-driven, no CLI parsing. Drover shells out per command. That's why Drover can't offer workspace navigation UI — the CLI surface it drives doesn't expose it, while both others have full create/focus/rename/split/close on workspaces/tabs/panes.

**Whip's core design is the most disciplined of the three**: all herdr JSON stays in Rust; React Native only receives typed versioned projections and sends semantic operations. One `HostRuntime` per host as sole owner of the session. Binary framing on the terminal hot path (no JSON serialization per frame). This reads like a desktop-grade client architecture — the tradeoff is the RN UI layer on top.

**Heeler's differentiators**: the real libghostty terminal (Metal-rendered, native scrollback — the best actual terminal view of any client here), a serious ADR paper trail (16 ADRs documenting every transport/security decision, including *why* it left Citadel: their pinned swift-nio-ssh got switched to an "unaudited fork" upstream — same concern Multiplex documents), and per-hop session drivers for nested jump hosts.

## Transcript/chat rendering

| | Heeler | Whip | Drover |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chat-model history | No native transcript reader — reads **pane text** via `agent read`/`pane.read` (visible/recent, 1000-line cap, no server-side scroll offsets) | **Native transcripts in Rust**: OpenCode via `opencode export` snapshot + `opencode db` incremental polling; Codex via rollout JSONL tail-follow — messages/thinking/tools/diffs, same SSH connection | Native JSONL over SFTP for Claude/Copilot/Codex/Pi/**omp** (512KiB bounded window, pull-to-load-more) + pane-text fallback |
| omp support | indirect (pane view only) | **no omp** — only Codex + OpenCode Chat View | **first-class omp** adapter |

This matters for you specifically: **Drover is the only one that parses omp session JSONL natively**. Whip's Chat View doesn't know omp at all; Heeler gives you the real terminal instead of a chat render. So despite Heeler/Whip being more mature transports, for *omp supervision as chat*, Drover's agent coverage is currently the best of the three — and it's the one whose omp integration hook I installed on your devbox an hour ago.

## Notifications & security model

| | Heeler | Whip | Drover |
|---|---|---|---|
| Push when app closed | **E2E AES-256-GCM** (per-host key; relay = stateless Cloudflare Worker holding only an APNs .p8 — never sees content) + **Live Activities** (Dynamic Island/lock screen, hybrid counts-plaintext/agent-details-encrypted) | **No remote push** — local on-device notifications/speech only; blocked/done alerts work while foregrounded | Firebase FCM via host-side plugin POST; **plaintext** `{hostId,paneId,agentName}` to Google's Firebase project; only credentials hashed |
| Key handling | Ed25519 generated on-device, private in Keychain; QR pairing with **single-use 2-minute bootstrap key + forced-command enrollment, self-revoking** | On-device key gen + **WP4 QR**: one-shot restricted credential, host-key pin verified before sending anything, 6-digit mutual verification code | You paste the PEM in (what we did) |
| Relay trust | relay sees only ciphertext + counts; custom relay URL supported if self-built | no relay exists — nothing to trust | Firebase project sees event metadata in cleartext |

Heeler's notification design is the strongest: E2E-encrypted content, a stateless relay that holds nothing, and honest ADR documentation of the Live Activity compromise (counts are cleartext to Apple because iOS offers no service-extension hook there). Whip has the cleanest *absence* of trust surface — but you get zero push when the app is killed, which on an iPhone (app suspension being what it is) means you'll miss blocked-agent alerts in practice. Drover's push works but is the most leaky design of the three.

## Maturity and host friction

| | Heeler | Whip | Drover |
|---|---|---|---|
| iOS availability | App Store + TestFlight, free | **No installable iOS build** — CI produces unsigned compile-validation artifacts only; you must run your own Xcode signed build (7-day expiry with free Apple ID) | App Store |
| Host-side requirements | herdr ≥0.7.5, Node ≥20 (plugin for pairing/notify), **stream-local forwarding allowed** (OpenSSH default) | SSH only; herdr optional (works with bare sshd) | herdr ≥0.8.0, Node ≥18 for notify plugin |
| Test/eng discipline | ADRs + testloop reports, CI | ~900 test files, CodeQL, actionlint — most rigorous | moderate |
| Documented rough edges | port fixed at 22 in pairing; no push-to-start Live Activities; remote history not addressable (1000-line pane cap) | iOS effectively a self-build project; session fallbacks don't survive app restart | shift+tab key injection broken ≤0.8.2 (uses raw backtab workaround); integration must predate session start; only `blocked` notifications shipped |

## Bottom line for you

- **Whip is out on practical grounds** — its internals are arguably the best-engineered, but there is no installable iOS build; you'd be maintaining an Xcode signing pipeline.
- **Heeler vs Drover is a real tradeoff**: Heeler wins on transport (real socket API + event stream → correct workspace/agent UI), terminal quality (libghostty), security (E2E push, proper on-device key with self-revoking pairing), and engineering maturity. Drover wins on the one axis you actually use: **first-class omp chat + permission buttons**, which Heeler doesn't model (pane-text only) and Whip doesn't support at all.
- Since both are free and use independent SSH keys, running Heeler *alongside* Drover costs nothing: Heeler for notifications + console + real-terminal access, Drover for omp chat/prompts. The two host-side plugins (`heeler.pair`, `drover.notify`) coexist fine.

If you want, I can install Heeler's pairing plugin on the devbox now (`herdr plugin install ZingerLittleBee/Heeler/plugin --ref main --yes`) so the QR is ready when you install the app — that's the only host-side step.

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code working in the drover repo. Complements (does not restate) the
global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` rules — those still apply.

## Repo layout

- `app/` — the Flutter app (iOS/macOS) plus `app/tool/spike.dart`, a CLI probe for the SSH/herdr path.

See `README.md` for the concept and layout, `docs/herdr-notes.md` for herdr
CLI behaviours/gotchas drover relies on, and `docs/agents/` for per-agent CLI
notes (`claude-notes.md`, `copilot-notes.md`, `codex-notes.md`,
`pi-notes.md`, `omp-notes.md`).

## One-time host setup

- [Flutter](https://flutter.dev), pinned via [fvm](https://fvm.app) to 3.47.2 (see
  `app/.fvmrc`): `dart pub global activate fvm`
- [marionette_mcp](https://pub.dev/packages/marionette_mcp) (lets Claude Code
  inspect/tap/screenshot the running app via the Dart VM service): `dart pub global
  activate marionette_mcp`, then ensure `~/.pub-cache/bin` is on PATH.
- [`asc`](https://asccli.sh) (starts Xcode Cloud builds — only needed to
  release): `brew install asc`, then `asc auth login --name drover --key-id …
  --issuer-id … --private-key …p8`. An App Store Connect API key with the
  **Developer** role is enough. Credentials go to the system keychain, so the
  `.p8` can be deleted afterwards.
- [git-cliff](https://git-cliff.org) (generates `CHANGELOG.md` entries — only
  needed for `just tag-release`, run after a version actually ships):
  `brew install git-cliff`.
- [`jq`](https://jqlang.org) (reads the App Store version state in
  `just tag-release` — only needed for that recipe): `brew install jq`.
- On the Herdr host (the SSH target running your agents): install a herdr
  integration for each agent you want native transcript history for:
  `herdr integration install claude`, `herdr integration install codex`,
  `herdr integration install copilot`, `herdr integration install pi`,
  `herdr integration install omp`.
  Without an integration, drover falls back to pane-text history. See
  `docs/herdr-notes.md` for the gotchas — notably, it only takes effect for
  sessions started after the install. For Codex specifically, the first
  launch after install may show a Hooks review panel; trust/enable the hook
  there, then start a fresh session.

## Marionette MCP

Register the server with Claude Code once:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport stdio marionette -- marionette_mcp
```

To control a local app, start it in debug mode, then copy the `ws://.../ws`
Dart VM service URI printed by `flutter run`. Call `marionette-connect` with
that URI before using its inspection or interaction tools.

## Key commands

A `justfile` wraps the app commands below (`just` to list recipes).

```sh
cd app
fvm flutter pub get
fvm flutter analyze
fvm flutter test
fvm flutter run
fvm flutter gen-l10n # regenerate localizations after editing lib/l10n/*.arb
fvm dart run tool/spike.dart --host <host> agents
```

## Releasing

The Xcode Cloud workflow is **manual-start only** — pushing builds nothing. Bump
the version and start a build in one step, from `main`:

```sh
just release        # 1.0.0+48 -> 1.0.0+49, same version, next build
just release 1.0.1  # 1.0.0+48 -> 1.0.1+49, new App Store version
```

Once a marketing version has actually been released on the App Store (state
`READY_FOR_DISTRIBUTION`), Apple closes that version's pre-release train for
new build uploads entirely — TestFlight-only iteration is **not** exempt
(confirmed 2026-08-09: a build-only bump on an already-released 1.0.0 failed
with ITMS-90186 "Invalid Pre-Release Train" + ITMS-90062). Plain `just release`
only works while the current marketing version hasn't shipped yet; once it has,
the next release needs a new semver.

`just release` never touches `CHANGELOG.md` or tags — it only starts a build,
and a build can be rejected or resubmitted before it actually ships. Once
`asc versions list` (or the App Store Connect dashboard) shows the target
semver as `READY_FOR_DISTRIBUTION`, record it:

```sh
just tag-release 1.0.1
```

`tag-release` re-checks that state itself, then asks App Store Connect which
Xcode Cloud build run actually produced the approved build and tags *that*
commit — not `HEAD`, which may have moved on while the build sat in review,
and not just "the last commit that bumped pubspec to this version": Xcode
Cloud assigns the shipped build number from its own counter, which doesn't
always match the number `just release` last wrote to `app/pubspec.yaml`. It
then generates a `CHANGELOG.md` section from the Conventional Commits since
the previous release tag and commits it separately on top of current `main`,
so the entry lands after the tagged commit rather than inside it. See
`cliff.toml` for the commit grouping/skip rules.

## UI previews

All previews run against a stubbed herdr backend (no SSH host needed) so you
can screenshot/inspect UI on a simulator. `just preview` opens an in-app
gallery listing every registered screen; `just preview <name>` (e.g.
`just preview launch`) boots one screen directly, which is handy for
marionette-driven screenshots. Pick a scenario via
`--dart-define=SCENARIO=idle|blocked` (default `idle`). The harness is a single
entrypoint `app/lib/previews/preview.dart` plus `app/lib/src/demo/demo_herdr.dart`,
and shares `droverTheme` and l10n with production. To add a screen, register a

content.text:
No more research needed — I have everything from the internals reports. Four answers:

## 1. omp integration + background notifications, no relay

The hard truth first: **any iOS push notification passes through APNs (Apple) — there is no such thing as relay-free background push on iOS.** The real question is who stands between your devbox and APNs:

| | omp native chat | Background push | What the middleman sees | Self-hostable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Drover** | ✅ first-class | Firebase Functions + FCM | `{hostId,paneId,agentName}` **cleartext** to the Firebase project | Firebase = effectively not self-hostable |
| **Heeler** | ❌ pane-text only | Cloudflare Worker relay → APNs | **ciphertext only** (AES-256-GCM, key never leaves your devices/host); relay is stateless, ~200 LOC, in-repo | ✅ **relay is open source and the app supports a custom relay URL** — you can run it on your devbox |
| **Whip** | ❌ | **none** — local alerts die when the app suspends | n/a | n/a (no feature to host) |

Given your constraint "no relay unless no other way": Heeler is the correct answer — it's relay-*minimal*. APNs is unavoidable, but you can eliminate every other third party: the relay code is in the repo, the app accepts a custom relay URL, so plugin → **your devbox-hosted relay** → APNs is a fully self-controlled path where the only party seeing anything is Apple, and even Apple's delivery payload is E2E-encrypted (the service-extension decrypts on-device). Drover's Firebase path can't be de-Googled realistically. Whip simply has no background notifications at all.

The gap: Heeler lacks omp chat. But note it renders the omp pane through libghostty, which is a *complete* view — just not chat-abstracted. Your priorities are split across two apps today: **Drover for omp chat, Heeler for trustworthy push.** They coexist; each installs its own host plugin and SSH key.

## 2. Chat vs terminal — when to use which

- **Chat model** (Drover's whole app; Heeler's Composer; Whip's Chat View): reviewing what an agent did across a long turn (markdown, diffs, tool calls without shell noise), answering permission prompts as buttons (no typo risk), sending follow-ups with autocorrect/dictation, triaging "which agent needs me" from status. Use it for *supervision and steering* — 80% of phone interaction.
- **Terminal** (Heeler libghostty, Whip xterm, Multiplex SwiftTerm): the moment the abstraction leaks — interactive pickers (`/model`, `/effort` menus that chat renderers can't show), agent crashed or wedged mid-turn, raw output the parser mangles (omp's spinner frames, TUI dialogs with no numbered options), running your own shell commands in the agent's cwd, scrolling history beyond what `pane read`'s 1000-line cap exposes. Use it for *debugging and anything structured parsers don't know*.
- Practical tell: if you ever find yourself sending Esc/arrow keys through a chat key-row (Drover 1.0.4 added exactly that as a stopgap), you wanted a terminal.

## 3. Building Whip yourself: Apple developer account

You do **not** need the paid $99/yr account — a **free Apple ID** can sign apps for your own device via Xcode. Two real catches:

1. **Free-Apple-ID signing expires every 7 days** — you rebuild + reinstall weekly (Heeler's README documents the same 7-day limit; Whip's README confirms its device script is the intended path). Paid account = 1-year signing, no other difference for personal use.
2. **The actual blocker is macOS**: Xcode only runs on a Mac. Your inventory is an iPhone + a Linux devbox. No Mac → you cannot build *any* of these (Whip, Heeler, Drover self-builds) locally. Workarounds: a cloud Mac (Codemagic/MacinCloud ~$), or a friend's Mac once to set up. Given Heeler is already on the App Store + TestFlight for free, self-building Whip to gain a chat view it doesn't have for omp anyway is a lot of ceremony for negative omp value — I'd rule it out.

## 4. Adding missing features — least work + which project welcomes contributions

**Least work to *your* feature set: Drover, decisively.** Its architecture is built for exactly this (compile-time `AgentAdapter` registry with per-agent capability negotiation, `agent_registry.dart`):

- omp native chat: **already exists** — your #1 requirement.
- `done` notifications: the plugin schema and `notifyOnDone` field already exist; the shipped plugin just only sends `blocked` — a ~10-line contribution.
- Workspace/session navigation: the CLI client already has `workspace list/create/rename` wired — adding a picker screen is small UI work, no new plumbing.
- The relay problem: replacing Firebase Functions with a self-hostable ~200-line HTTPS endpoint (Heeler's relay is the reference design) is the one *moderate* item.

**Adding omp chat to Heeler**, by contrast, means building an entire native-transcript layer it deliberately doesn't have (SFTP jsonl reader + parser + chat renderer + the structured-prompt key-injection machinery Drover spent most of its complexity budget on). That's the biggest single feature gap across all four projects — feasible (Drover's MIT code is a direct reference), but weeks, not days.

**Openness / contribution velocity:**

- **Heeler** — the most genuinely open project of the four: 324★, 22 forks, ADR paper trail, dated testloop reports (the repo shows reports through 2026-09-13 — yesterday), CONTRIBUTING.md with real conventions, Trendshift badge, and an architecture (`Transport` abstraction, UI never touches SSH) that makes PRs reviewable. Apache 2.0.
- **Drover** — tiny community (4★, solo dev), but shipping fast (1.0.0 → 1.0.5 in five weeks) and the smallest, simplest codebase; a solo maintainer merging quickly is common at this stage. MIT. For *small* contributions (done-notifications, a workspace picker), response probability is good.
- **Whip** — the most rigorous (900 test files, CodeQL, actionlint) but Android-first with iOS explicitly a "future milestone": your iOS-facing PRs would land on a maintainer who doesn't prioritize that surface, and AGPL narrows who can reuse your work. Worst contribution ROI for you.

**Recommendation:** contribute to **Drover** — it's the app whose feature set matches your priorities, with the smallest missing-delta (self-hostable/no-Google push path + `done` events + workspace picker). Run **Heeler from the App Store** in parallel for E2E push + real terminal. If the Drover relay work goes well and you later want everything in one app, porting Drover's omp transcript layer into Heeler is the natural follow-up — but only worth it after you've lived with both for a while.

One thing I'd do right now, before any of that: install Heeler's host plugin and pair it, so you have working background push this week (its setup is one `herdr plugin install` + a QR scan) — say the word and I'll run the host side.

Plugin installed (v0.4.0, from Heeler main @ `5e22c43`, enabled; Node v24.20.0 satisfies the ≥20 requirement). It registered the pairing action, the popup pane, and both notification hooks (`notify-hook.js` + `activity-hook.js` on `pane.agent_status_changed`) — so push notifications are already wired host-side; they activate once you pair and enable them in the app.

**How to pair — 4 steps:**

1. **Install Heeler on the iPhone** — App Store ([Heeler for herdr](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/heeler-for-herdr/id6797263135)); if it's not available in your country's store, use their TestFlight: `https://testflight.apple.com/join/aXSxRn4r`.

2. **Generate the QR** — from any shell on the devbox (including from Drover), run:
   ```bash
   herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair
   ```
   This opens a herdr popup pane rendering the QR code.

3. **Scan it from Heeler** — Heeler's first-run screen → Add Host → scan. The QR carries: candidate addresses + port 22, your username, the devbox's host-key fingerprint (pinned — no trust-on-first-use guess), plus a **single-use Ed25519 bootstrap key that self-expires in 2 minutes** and is revoked the moment enrollment succeeds.

4. **In Heeler, enable notifications for that host** — Heeler writes its push token + the per-host Notification Key (AES-256-GCM) into the plugin config over SSH. From then on, blocked/done agent events on this devbox reach your phone E2E-encrypted through the relay.

Two gotchas to know:

- **The QR is time-limited and one-shot** — do steps 2–3 back-to-back; if it expires, just re-invoke the action. And treat the QR as secret-while-displayed (anyone photographing it in the 2-minute window could race the enrollment — that's the accepted risk in their design, fine at home).
- **Pairing assumes the iPhone can reach the devbox's SSH port directly** (same LAN/VPN) — same requirement Drover already proved works, so nothing new here.
- The app's Device Key is generated on-device and lands in your `authorized_keys` as its own line — your Drover PEM entry stays untouched; the two coexist.

One optional follow-up while you're at it: if you want the *self-hosted relay* (no third party at all beyond Apple), tell me and I'll set up the Cloudflare-Workers-compatible relay on this devbox — the app supports a custom relay URL, but only in a self-built app (App Store builds point at the author's relay, which only ever sees ciphertext anyway). For now, the author's relay + E2E encryption is the pragmatic default.

content.text:
Straight from the internals dug up earlier — different answers for each:

**Heeler: no native session parsing at all, so no registration requirement — and no benefit either.** It never reads agent JSONL files; its transcript view is herdr's **pane text** (`agent read`/`pane.read`, bounded by herdr's retained buffer, ~1000-line cap, no scrollback offsets). That data exists for *every* pane regardless of integrations, so an agent started last week and one started now look the same in Heeler. The tradeoff: you get the TUI-as-text render (omp spinner frames, redraws, etc.), not a chat abstraction. Heeler deliberately built the Composer around this because herdr's API offered no addressable remote history (their ADR-0012 documents this exact reasoning).

**Whip: same integration-before-start constraint as Drover, for the agents it supports.** Its Chat View resolves transcripts *through herdr's `agent_session` field* — the Rust core takes the pane's `agent_session` ID, then reads the OpenCode durable events / Codex rollout JSONL over SSH. `agent_session` is exactly what the integration hook registers at session start — so a Codex/OpenCode session started before `herdr integration install codex`/`opencode` has no registration, and Whip's Chat View has nothing to resolve. Same limitation, same fix (bounce + restart under the hook). And of course its Chat View covers only Codex + OpenCode — not omp, which is your agent.

So ranked for "give me chat history for already-running omp sessions without ceremony":

1. **Drover** — omp supported natively; needs the one-time integration + restart, which we've now done for your idle agents. Only the two still-working ones pending.
2. **Whip** — native parsing, but not omp, and same registration constraint (plus no installable iOS build).
3. **Heeler** — no constraint because no native parsing; you always see *something*, but never chat-model history.

The structural reason, worth knowing: herdr itself only learns an agent's session file via the integration hooks (that's the `agent_session` field everything keys off). Any client that parses native transcripts — Drover today, Whip for its two agents, and any future Heeler feature — inherits the "integration must predate session start" rule. There's no client-side way around it; the session-to-jsonl mapping simply doesn't exist in herdr's state otherwise.

# omp agent notes

Behaviours of the **omp** CLI ("Oh My Pi", the successor/rebrand of `pi`) that
drover's omp adapter depends on, as observed over herdr. For herdr's own
behaviours (which apply to every agent — workspace handling, the `shift+tab`
encoding bug, the text-only input channel, the `agent_session` mechanism), see
`../herdr-notes.md`.

Observed against **omp v18.1.11** and **herdr integration omp v8** unless noted
otherwise.

omp's adapter reuses pi's transcript parser and loader
(`app/lib/src/agents/pi/pi_transcript.dart`, parameterized by agent name), so
this file deliberately does **not** re-derive pi's observations. Where omp is
identical it cross-references `pi-notes.md`; what follows are the differences
and the newly verified facts. omp's help text still names its environment as
`PI_*` (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` — "Session storage directory (default:
`~/.omp/agent`)", `PI_SMOL_MODEL`, `PI_SLOW_MODEL`, `PI_PLAN_MODEL`,
`PI_NO_PTY`), plus `OMP_PROFILE`.

## Native transcript source (`agent_session`)

- **omp reports its transcript as a path, like pi and unlike claude, codex
  and copilot.** (2026-09-06) The general `agent_session` mechanism (integration
  required, only from the next `SessionStart`, fallback to pane-text history)
  is in `../herdr-notes.md`; the `kind:'path'` consequences — no remote
  lookup, path validation plus a once-per-session SFTP readability probe, and
  the silent degrade to pane-text history when that probe fails — are in
  `pi-notes.md` and hold unchanged for omp. Live from
  `herdr agent start ompprobe --kind omp`:

  ```
  {source:'herdr:omp', agent:'omp', kind:'path',
   value:'/Users/administrator/.omp/agent/sessions/-Projects-drover-main/2026-09-06T08-53-01-667Z_01a075eb-c863-74fc-85a7-2158948439fb.jsonl'}
  ```

- **The integration installs under a different filename from pi's, so the two
  coexist.** (2026-09-06) `herdr integration install omp` writes a TypeScript
  extension to `~/.omp/agent/extensions/herdr-omp-agent-state.ts`, where pi's
  lives at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/herdr-agent-state.ts`. Installing one does
  not disturb the other. Like every herdr integration it only takes effect for
  sessions started **after** the install — see `../herdr-notes.md`.

- **Session-file layout (background only).** (2026-09-06) Session files live at
  `${PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR:-$HOME/.omp/agent}/sessions/<slugified-cwd>/<ISO-timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl`.
  The slug rule differs from pi's: omp produced `-Projects-drover-main` where
  pi produced `--Users-administrator-Projects-drover-main--` for the same
  directory. drover never constructs this path — herdr reports it — but it is
  recorded here so nobody reuses pi's slug rule for omp.

## Windows divergence: a path drover declines

- **On a Windows herdr host omp *does* report `kind:'path'`, and drover
  rejects it.** (2026-09-06) pi's extension only reports a path when it passes
  `file.startsWith("/")`, so on a Windows host pi silently degrades to
  reporting a session id (`kind:'id'`) — see pi-notes' "Windows fallback
  (`kind:'id'`)". omp's v8 extension instead uses `isAbsoluteSessionPath()` =
  `path.posix.isAbsolute(file) || path.win32.isAbsolute(file)`, so a Windows
  host yields `kind:'path'` with a `C:\…` value. drover's
  `_isSafeTranscriptPath` requires a leading `/`, so it declines that value and
  the pane falls back to the generic ANSI pane-text transcript. The phase-1
  outcome matches pi's, but the **reason is the opposite**: pi never offers a
  path on Windows; omp offers one drover refuses. drover has shipped Windows-
  host support, so this path is reachable rather than hypothetical. Known,
  deliberate limitation, not a bug to chase; the upgrade path is to accept a
  Windows-absolute path in the validator.

## Transcript record types

- **Record shapes are identical to pi's.** (2026-09-06) `type:'message'`
  records with `message.role` in `user`/`assistant`/`toolResult`/
  `bashExecution`; content blocks `{type:'text'}`, `{type:'thinking'}`,
  `{type:'toolCall', id, name, arguments}`; a tool result is its own top-level
  record carrying `toolCallId`/`toolName`/`isError`/`content`, paired to its
  call by `toolCallId`. See `pi-notes.md` for the block-by-block detail,
  including the "iterate every content block" warning — it applies unchanged.

- **`toolCall.arguments` is already a decoded JSON object.** (2026-09-06) Same
  as pi, and unlike Codex's JSON-*encoded* string (see `codex-notes.md`). Do
  not re-decode.

- **New non-`message` top-level types beyond pi's set.** (2026-09-06) Observed
  in omp session files: `title`, `title_change`, `custom_message` (seen with
  `customType:'xdev-mount-notice'`), and `custom` with `customType` of
  `tool_execution_start` and `session_exit`. All are skipped by the parser's
  existing "top-level `type` is not `message`" guard, so no parser change was
  needed — recorded here so that guard's coverage is visible rather than
  accidental.

- **`toolCallId` is long and contains a `|`.** (2026-09-06) Real example,
  truncated:
  `call_CDXPvNPA1U69hZtEFTn5UoJR|y+sSKRvAXV0DDruBd8sDCuDVacPSg9kbIpsu/ionw…`
  — several hundred characters, apparently a provider reasoning payload
  appended after the pipe. Harmless as an opaque pairing key, but do not assume
  a short id.

## Unsupported capabilities

All three stay null on the omp adapter, as for pi — but partly for different
reasons.

- **Interaction mode: `AgentModeCapability` is null.** (2026-09-06) A
  `shift+tab` keystroke in a live omp pane cycles the **thinking level**, not
  an interaction mode — corroborated independently by the
  `thinking_level_change` records the same actions wrote to the session file.
  omp does have approval modes (`--approval-mode always-ask|write|yolo`), but
  they are a launch flag, not a status-line mode drover can read or cycle, and
  omp's status bar carries no mode line to parse. So there is nothing to map.

- **Structured prompts: `StructuredPromptCapability` is null — and unlike pi,
  this one is verified.** (2026-09-06) omp ships an `ask` tool enabled by
  default (a different tool from pi's `ask_question`, whose record shape and
  dialog remain unverified — see `pi-notes.md`). Prompting a live pane to use
  it produced an assistant `toolCall` named `ask` with arguments shaped like:

  ```json
  {"i":"Asking color preference","questions":[{"id":"color_preference","question":"Which color do you prefer?","options":[{"label":"Red","description":null,"preview":null}],"header":null,"multi":null,"recommended":null}]}
  ```

  and a TUI dialog whose footer reads
  `Enter select · n note · ↑/↓ move · Esc cancel`. The options are **not
  numbered** — selection is by arrow keys. AgentScreen's generic pane-text
  fallback parses *numbered* prompts, so it does not detect an omp `ask`: the
  pane goes `blocked` and the question has to be answered with arrow keys in
  the live terminal. Known limitation, not a bug to chase; a real
  `StructuredPromptCapability` for omp is separate work.

- **Image attachments: `ImageAttachmentCapability` is null.** (2026-09-06) omp
  takes file references as `@path` arguments (`omp @prompt.md @image.png "…"`);
  whether typing a literal `@/abs/path` into the TUI composer behaves the same
  way rather than triggering its autocomplete is **not verified**, so the
  composer's attach-image affordance is hidden for omp.

## Terminal title and avatar

- **omp's terminal title IS a conversation summary — unlike pi's.**
  (2026-09-06) pi sets `π - <directory name>` (see `pi-notes.md`); omp sets
  `π > <summary>`. Verified: a fresh pane showed `π > main`, and after one
  prompt it became `π > Reply exactly hello from omp`. So
  `AgentInfo.sessionTitle` is genuinely useful for an omp pane, where for pi it
  is only a directory name. While a pane was blocked on `ask`, the title was
  observed with a `!` marker instead: `π ! Reply exactly hello from omp`.

- **omp has no explicit avatar case arm, and that is deliberate.**
  (2026-09-06) `AgentAvatar`'s fallback takes the first letter of the agent
  type, giving `O` — which collides with nothing among claude (`C`), codex
  (`X`), copilot (`P`) and pi (`π`). Stated explicitly so nobody "fixes" the
  missing arm later. omp's own glyph is `π`, but pi already claims it.

- **Brand color `Color(0xFF55AAB9)`.** (2026-09-06) A cyan-blue at OKLCH hue
  210, chosen to sit in the same lightness/chroma band as the existing five
  while taking the largest free hue gap, between codex (161) and copilot (267).

Both symptoms explained — I've now read the actual Drover source (cloned to `/tmp/drover-src`):

## "Both terminal and chats are showing" — that's by design, not a bug

`agent_screen.dart` renders the screen as **native chat history + a "Live terminal" section appended at the bottom**. When native history exists, `_liveTerminalText()` returns the pane tail *unless* it duplicates recent chat content (there's a dedup heuristic — a large overlap threshold hides the terminal section). So seeing chat with a live-terminal panel below it is the intended layout: chat = parsed jsonl history; live terminal = the current pane bytes (ANSI-faithful, includes what the chat parser hasn't caught up to). The terminal section auto-hides only when it substantially duplicates the chat tail. If the current turn is mid-flight (spinner frames, partial tool output not yet in the jsonl, or content the parser skips), dedup fails → both sections show. Nothing is wrong; that's the design covering the gap between the two data sources.

## "Half parsed — history chats parsed, latest rounds not" — the 512KiB window boundary, confirmed numerically

The parser skips the *leading partial record* of its bounded window, but there's a second property: **the initial load fetches only the last 512KiB** of the jsonl (`nativeTranscriptWindowBytes = 512 * 1024` in `native_transcript.dart`). Your current session's jsonl:

- Total: **1.19 MB**, 517 lines
- 512KiB window starts at **line 374, timestamp 10:46 UTC** — which lands mid-way through this very conversation, right around the "other iOS herdr clients comparison" turns

So Drover's chat shows everything from ~"btw, you found other ios herdr clients?" onward... wait, actually the *tail* is what loads, so you see the RECENT half in chat — the boundary at line 374 means the chat starts mid-conversation (around the client-comparison turns) and everything before that is behind **pull-to-load-older** (the `loadOlder` fetch of earlier bounded chunks). "Latest rounds not parsed" in your report + the timestamps suggest the inverse: if what you're seeing is *old* content in chat but not the newest turns, that's the **append-poll** half: after the initial load, Drover only picks up new records via polling `bytes appended since last read`. While a turn is active, omp appends continuously and the poll should follow — but if the poll hit one of its known failure modes (the once-per-session SFTP readability probe, a path re-validation, or simply the app having cached the load before the file grew past a boundary), it stops appending and the Live terminal covers the gap instead — which is exactly "chat renders old rounds, terminal shows the new ones."

Since I have the running state here, the concrete check: the file is actively growing (every turn appends). If Drover's chat is frozen at a specific turn while the terminal shows newer ones, force a re-fetch in the app: pull-to-refresh the transcript (or back out of the agent and reopen it — the native-history cache is per-pane but re-loads on a fresh `AgentScreen`). If it's instead showing everything up to "now − N turns" and the oldest history is what's missing, that's just the window — pull to load older.

If it recurs on the *current* session specifically, there's one structural cause worth knowing: **this session has no duplicate writers anymore** (verified — one omp owns the jsonl, no stale `--resume` copies), so it's not corruption; it's the windowing/polling behavior above. The 512KiB initial window will keep biting long conversations like this one (1.2 MB already) — pull-to-load-older is the designed remedy, and the append-poll keeps it current from there.

I've mapped your feature list against the actual Drover source (cloned at `/tmp/drover-src`). Verdict up front: **fork Drover**. Here's the feature-by-feature grounding and the one hard blocker you need to solve first.

## Base choice: Drover (MIT) — it's the only base with your #1 feature

- omp chat parsing exists nowhere else. Drover's `pi_transcript.dart` parser (omp reuses it, parameterized) + `omp_adapter.dart` + `AgentAdapter` capability registry covers omp/pi/Claude/Codex/Copilot with native JSONL→chat. Heeler has no chat parser; Whip has none for omp; Multiplex is terminal-only. Rebuilding that on any other base = the biggest single chunk of work, for free in Drover.
- MIT license: fork, modify, keep private, no copyleft. (Whip is AGPL — fork would force open-sourcing; Heeler Apache-2.0 is fine but you'd start without the chat layer.)
- You already run it and know its UX gaps — your list is essentially "Drover minus my complaints."

## Feature-by-feature: what exists, what you build

| Feature | Status in Drover | Your work |
|---|---|---|
| **omp chat history** | ✅ complete (parser, adapter, 512KiB window, loadOlder paging, append-poll) | none; fix the window size if 512KiB annoys you (one constant) |
| **Maximal chat area, minimal chrome** | ❌ M3-style app bar, Material widgets | UI rewrite of `agent_screen.dart` — pure Flutter layout work, no plumbing |
| **Detail levels (overview default, hide thinking/edit/diff/toolcall)** | Partial: `TranscriptMessage/Thinking/ToolUse/ToolResult` models already separate every record type; today it renders all | New collapsible renderer: level 0 = assistant text turns only (you have this data — `type:'text'` blocks, already parsed); levels 1–3 reveal tool calls/diffs/thinking. The data model makes this cheap; it's a render-layer feature |
| **Blended hosts/sessions/workspaces** | Hosts: ✅ (`HostsState`, `HerdScreen` polls all hosts, `filterHostId`) · Workspaces: ✅ (`listWorkspaces`, per-agent `workspace_id`) · **Named sessions: ❌** — every CLI call assumes the default session | Add a session dimension: each poll issues `herdr --session <name> agent list`. Since Drover is CLI-driven (exec per command), this is a flag threaded through `herdr_client.dart` + a session lister per host (`herdr session list --json`) — mechanical, contained |
| **Keyboard enhancement** | Basic key row (added 1.0.4) | New: swipe/long-press chord layer, per-agent key macros — pure UI |
| **Input integration (`/`, `#`, `@`, `!`)** | ❌ plain composer | New composer tokenizer. `@` = agent/pane mention → route prompt to that pane; `!` = shell exec via `pane run`; `/` = omp slash commands; `#` = tag/search. The herdr client already has `pane send-text/run` and `agent prompt` — this is a routing layer over existing primitives |
| **URI/file opener** | Partial: SFTP `readFile`/`statFile`/`uploadFile` exist (transcript + image paths already flow remote↔local) | New viewers: in-app markdown render (Flutter packages exist), URL open (SFSafariViewController / external), editor = local file download → edit → SFTP push back. The silent remote→local transfer machinery (`CommandRunner.readFile`) is already there |
| **Background/closed notifications** | ⚠️ Firebase relay — the part you reject | Rip out `functions/` + FCM; adopt **Heeler's model**: host-side herdr plugin (Drover already has the plugin skeleton `drover-notify`, zero npm deps) → your devbox-hosted stateless relay (Heeler's `relay/` is ~200 LOC Cloudflare-Workers-compatible, MIT-compatible Apache-2.0 reference) → APNs with **E2E AES-256-GCM** payloads (Heeler's `docs/agents/live-activity-contract.md` is a full wire spec). This is the second-largest work item |

## The hard blocker first: you have no Mac

Building *any* iOS client requires Xcode. iPhone + Linux devbox can't compile iOS. Options:

1. **Codemagic CI** (Flutter-native, what Drover-style projects use) — free tier 500 min/mo, builds + signs + TestFlight-distributes from git push. For a Flutter fork this is the path of least resistance.
2. GitHub Actions macOS runners (2,000 min/mo on Pro plan).
3. Borrow a Mac once for provisioning-profile bootstrap, then CI for everything.

And the inescapable: **Apple Developer Program $99/yr** for real background push (APNs certificate + TestFlight distribution + >7-day signing). Free Apple ID gets you 7-day personal builds only, and *no APNs* — push is one of your requirements, so budget the $99.

## Suggested architecture inside the fork

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph iPhone["Your client (Drover fork)"]
    Chat[Chat renderer\nlevel 0-3 detail] --- Comp[Composer\n/ # @ ! router]
    Comp --> HC[HerdrClient\nCLI over dartssh2 + session flag]
    HC --> SFTP[SFTP read/write\nfiles + transcripts]
  end
  subgraph Devbox["herdr host(s), per session"]
    HC -->|"ssh exec + sftp"| H1[session: default]
    HC --> H2[session: main]
    PN[drover-notify fork\nE2E plugin] --> R[relay on devbox\nstateless]
  end
  R -->|AES-GCM ciphertext| APNs[Apple APNs] --> Chat
```

Keep Drover's CLI-over-SSH transport for v1 (works, you understand it); the socket-API upgrade (Heeler/Whip style, event stream instead of polling) is a v2 refactor behind the same `HerdrClient` interface — that interface seam is already clean (`CommandRunner` abstraction).

## Effort reality check

- v1 (fork + minimal chrome + detail levels + session blending): **2–4 weekends** — mostly familiar Flutter UI work, no new protocol knowledge.
- Composer input modes + file/URI openers: +1–2 weekends (all existing primitives).
- E2E self-hosted notifications: +1 weekend (port Heeler's spec; the crypto is one AES-GCM envelope), but **gated on Apple Developer account + CI signing working first**.

Sequencing that avoids the classic trap: **get CI signing + TestFlight loop working on the unmodified fork first** (proves the Mac-less pipeline), then UI features, then notifications last (most external dependencies).

One housekeeping note before you start: the fork diverges from upstream Drover, which is shipping weekly — cherry-pick strategy beats long-lived divergence; keep your changes layered (renderer, composer, notify) rather than scattered, so upstream merges stay cheap. And per your earlier interest in contributing back: the detail-levels renderer and session blending are exactly the kind of upstream-able features a 4★ solo maintainer would likely welcome — worth PR'ing instead of forking away, which also keeps your merge burden near zero.

So "notify me when the app is closed" cannot be implemented inside your own app at $0.

## The $0 workaround for closed-app notifications: push via a third-party app's APNs

You don't need your own APNs cert if you ride an app that already has one. Best fit: **Bark** (free iOS app, open-source server, self-hostable):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  H[herdr plugin on devbox\nblocked/done hook] -->|"HTTP localhost"| B[bark-server\nself-hosted on devbox]
  B -->|"APNs (Apple)"| A[Bark app on iPhone]
  A -.->|tap| H
```

- bark-server runs **on your devbox** — the "relay" is your own machine, which was your constraint ("no relay unless no other way" — APNs is genuinely the only way on iOS, and this minimizes it to Apple + the Bark app's cert; bark-server can't be cut out, the Bark app's key is what signs pushes).
- Bark supports encrypted push bodies (key set in-app), so the plaintext-visibility surface stays tiny.
- The host side is the same plugin shape as `drover-notify`/Heeler's notify-hook: hook on `pane.agent_status_changed` → POST to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/<your-bark-key>/Agent blocked: <title>`. A fork of drover-notify with the Firebase POST swapped for a localhost Bark POST is ~50 lines.
- Tradeoff: tapping the notification opens Bark, not your app (deep links into a free-signed app are unreliable). You'll tap Bark → open your app → the console shows who needs you. Acceptable for supervision alerts.

Alternative in the same class: Pushover ($5 one-time) — but its server is closed and sees plaintext; Bark self-hosted is strictly better for your trust model.

## Weekly build ritual (the cost of $0)

One command on the MacBook, automatable:

```bash
cd drover-fork/app
flutter build ios --debug --no-codesign   # or a small script:
xcodebuild -workspace Runner.xcworkspace -scheme Runner \
  -configuration Debug -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<personal-team-id>
# then install:
xcrun devicectl device install app <path-to-.app>  # USB-connected iPhone
```

Practical notes: keep the iPhone plugged in for install (or use Xcode's Devices window); do the free-team signing setup once in Xcode (it manages the provisioning profile); rebuild *before* day 7 or the app dies mid-flight — a Monday-morning habit is enough. You get 3 personal apps at a time, so your fork + two side-loaded others max — Drover and Heeler come from the Store/TestFlight and don't count.

## Forking & licensing — no friction

Drover is **MIT**: fork, keep private, no obligation, no upstream acceptance needed. Your stated preference (fork if PRs rejected) is exactly the license's default mode. Strategy stays: layer your changes (renderer / composer / notify-plugin) so weekly upstream cherry-picks from keinstn/drover stay cheap — the author ships weekly, and you'll want his bugfixes.

## Revised sequence

1. **Day 1**: fork Drover → unmodified build on the MacBook → install → connect to the devbox (reuse the PEM key; or better, a new key). Proves the toolchain.
2. **Week 1–2**: minimal-chrome chat layout + detail levels (levels 0–3 renderer; data model already separates thinking/toolcall/diff records — render-layer work).
3. **Week 2–3**: session blending (thread `--session` through `herdr_client.dart` + session lister per host) + composer input modes (`/ # @ !`).
4. **Week 3–4**: file/URI openers (SFTP plumbing exists; add markdown viewer + open-in-browser + local edit→push-back).
5. **Parallel, independent**: Bark on iPhone + bark-server on devbox + forked notify plugin → this doesn't touch the app at all, so you can have working closed-app notifications this week even before the fork builds.
6. Optional later: when you cave on $99 someday, swap Bark for direct APNs with Heeler's E2E design — the plugin shape stays identical, only the delivery endpoint changes.

Total: your feature list minus direct push, at $0, with one weekly command and one self-hosted ~200-line service. The only thing the $99 would buy back is first-party push and TestFlight convenience — nothing else on your list needs it.

## API reality this design is shaped by (verified live on herdr 0.8.0)

- Remote history is **not addressable**: `pane.read`/`agent.read` take only
  `visible`/`recent` and a line count — no offset, no cursor — with a server
  hard cap of 1000 lines. "Scroll to load older from the server" cannot exist.
- For alternate-screen TUIs (claude), history is capturable **only while the
  Agent is idle** (`agent_not_idle` otherwise); while working, only the
  current screen is readable.
--

  push signal Monitor uses.
- `agent.prompt` types text plus Enter and, without `wait`, returns
  immediately as a delivery acknowledgment. Prompting a working agent is
  accepted unconditionally; queueing is the agent TUI's behavior, not herdr's.

Hence the model: while working, Monitor mirrors the latest screen by adaptive
foreground polling; on idle/done it stops polling and follows status events;

Delivered, and subsequent status events carry the working→done story.
