Survey done — Heeler is now cloned at `/tmp/heeler-src` and I've mapped it file-by-file the same way I did Drover. Your hypothesis is correct, with one sharpening: **the missing piece on the Heeler path is the native agent-transcript (chat) layer, and it's the only large piece.** Verified numbers first, then the two-path comparison.

## What building on Heeler gets you (verified from source)

**Codebase**: 180 Swift files, **42.9k LOC** app + 3.4k (host plugin, JS) + 1.3k (push relay). Tests: **155 test files**. Layout: `Transport/` (7.5k — libssh2 direct-streamlocal onto `herdr.sock`, 18 socket-API methods: `agent.list/prompt/read/start/rename/send_keys`, `pane.read/close`, `workspace.*`, `tab.create`, `worktree.*`, `session.snapshot`, `ping`), `Terminal/` (6.3k, libghostty), `Console/` (15k, pane-text mirror UI), `Pairing/` (1.2k), `Notifications/`+`LiveActivities/` (3k, the done E2E push), `Skills/` (1.4k — it already *reads herdr agent skills*), `Snippets/` (483), `Attachments/` (SFTP staging, 648).

Against your feature list:

| Feature | Heeler status |
|---|---|
| Socket-API transport (your anti-CLI requirement) | ✅ done — this is Heeler's core, with 16 ADRs documenting channel budgets (`MaxSessions` 8+1), stream-local failure classification, jump-host nesting |
| Event stream (status changes pushed, no polling) | ✅ `subscribeToEvents` on a reserved channel |
| **Blended hosts/sessions** | ✅ **nearly free**: a `Host` entry pins one `sessionName` (blank = default) and `listSessions()` already exists — so devbox:default + devbox:main = two Host entries, zero code. Workspaces come free in `agent.list`. Cross-host blending is the console's existing model |
| Notifications (background/closed) | ✅ done host-side (plugin installed on your box already) — see caveat below |
| Chat view for omp | ❌ **the gap.** ADR-0012 documents why: herdr's `pane.read` is capped at 1000 lines, no offsets, alternate-screen agents only readable when idle — Heeler's answer was the pane-text Monitor. Drover's answer was better: **read the omp session JSONL over SFTP**. That's what you'd port |
| Keyboard/composer | Partial: native Composer with one-shot `agent.prompt` delivery exists; your `/ # @ !` router is new |
| File/URI openers | Partial: SFTP staging + Skills file reading exist; markdown viewer/browser/editor are new |
| Detail levels (overview default) | ❌ new — but it *comes with* the chat renderer you're porting |

## The critical caveat for BOTH paths: free Apple ID = no APNs on your fork

"Heeler's notification is already done" is true for the **upstream TestFlight build** (author's paid account signs its APNs). Your own fork, signed with a free personal team, **cannot get the `aps-environment` entitlement** — no push, regardless of base. So the play is: your fork (whatever it is) for the interactive app, and **upstream Heeler TestFlight stays installed as your notification surface** — its plugin is already on your devbox, its E2E push works today. Two binaries, two keys, same host, no conflict. (Alternative: Bark self-hosted, if you'd rather not run two Heelers.)

## Two paths compared (both: free Apple ID, weekly `make`/`xcodebuild`, agents write the code, you review design)

| | **A: Fork Drover (Flutter)** | **B: Fork Heeler (Swift)** |
|---|---|---|
| You get | omp chat parser done (the crown jewel, 3.1k LOC agents layer + documented record shapes in `omp-notes.md`); multi-host polling done | Transport done (7.5k LOC, event-driven, no CLI); sessions free; notifications architecture done; worktrees, jump hosts, QR pairing, SFTP, Skills/Snippets all done |
| You must build | ① **Transport rewrite** — replace CLI-over-exec with socket API. Risk: dartssh2's stream-local (Unix-socket forwarding) support is unverified `[INFERENCE — verify before choosing this path]`; if absent you're swapping SSH libraries or bridging via socat (Heeler's own deprecated v1 approach) ② session dimension via `--session` ③ Firebase → Bark/E2E removal ④ UI de-chroming ⑤ detail levels ⑥ composer modes ⑦ file openers | ① **Chat layer** — port Drover's parser to Swift (omp JSONL → message/thinking/toolCall models; reference impl is MIT, record spec documented), fetch via existing SFTP + `agent_session` from `agent.list` (the socket API exposes it — verified in your own `api snapshot` output), new SwiftUI chat screen with your detail levels baked in ② UI de-chroming ③ composer modes ④ file openers |
| Biggest build item | Transport — the *hard* part, and Heeler's ADRs prove how much subtlety it hides | Chat — the *additive* part, with a working reference implementation to port |
| Codebase to understand | 16.4k LOC Dart, 84 files, simple | 42.9k LOC Swift, 180 files — but you only touch `Console/` (add chat screen), `Transport/` (add transcript fetch), `Files/`; and the ADRs + `CONTEXT.md` + 155 test files mean the architecture is *explained in the repo* |
| Agent-driven development fit | Good: CLAUDE.md, marionette MCP for UI inspection, preview harness | **Better — this repo is literally built that way**: `.testloop/reports/` are dated agent test reports (latest yesterday), CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/ADR paper trail, `make install` targets your USB iPhone directly. Guardrails for "agents code, you review" are the strongest of the four clients |
| Merge-with-upstream future | Author ships weekly; your transport rewrite diverges hard from his | Your chat layer is *new modules* — upstream merges stay near-free; and chat is the feature most likely to be accepted upstream (Heeler has open issues asking for richer history) |
| License | MIT | Apache 2.0 — fork fine, keep NOTICE |
| Your build ritual | `flutter build` + devicectl | `make install` (repo-provided, auto-finds your iPhone) |

## Verdict: **Path B — build on Heeler**

Reasoning:
1. Your stated dislikes map exactly to what Heeler already solved (CLI → socket; notifications → done outside the fork). The one thing you must build (chat) is *additive* and has a reference implementation plus a written spec. On path A, the thing you must build (transport) is *foundational* — it touches every existing feature, hides the most subtlety, and has a library-support risk before it even starts.
2. For your working mode — no client-side coding, agents write, you review design — Heeler's repo is the best-shaped codebase of the four: architecture is pre-explained (ADRs/CONTEXT.md), tests exist, and the maintainer develops it the same way you will. Your review surface is two new modules, not a transport rewrite rippling through everything.
3. Sessions/workspaces blending — explicitly on your list — costs zero code on B, real code on A.
4. Upstream-merge economics favor B: your chat layer is isolated new code.

Sequenced plan for Path B:

1. **Week 0 (this week, unmodified)**: clone Heeler → change bundle ID → `make install` on your MacBook → connect to devbox (pairing QR works — plugin's already installed). Proves the free-signing toolchain before any code.
2. **Week 1–2 — chat layer**: port Drover's `pi_transcript.dart` parser to Swift (agents handle this well: the record shapes are documented in `omp-notes.md`, and your live devbox jsonls are perfect fixtures — real 1.2MB conversation files to test against). Add `Transport.readTranscriptFile` (SFTP), pull `agent_session` from `agent.list`. New `ChatScreen` with **detail levels designed in from the start** (level 0 = assistant text only — you get to decide the default, rather than retrofit).
3. **Week 2–3**: composer `/ # @ !` router (Heeler's Composer + `agent.prompt` are the primitives), minimal-chrome layout pass.
4. **Week 3–4**: file/URI openers on existing SFTP.
5. Notifications: nothing to build — upstream TestFlight Heeler keeps that duty.

One honest cost of B to weigh: as the reviewer you'll need *reading* fluency in Swift/SwiftUI where Drover would have been Dart. But since agents write and you review architecture/design, Heeler's ADR-disciplined structure actually makes that review *easier* than a smaller but undisciplined codebase — the reasoning is written down, you check code against it.

# Obsidian Vault Operations

Operate on the user's personal Obsidian vault at
`/home/jhou/Documents/obsidian-nvidia` ("the vault" hereafter). This structural
skill covers the flat `2-Notes/` note system, frontmatter schema, templates,
tasks, Bases views, search, and manual commits.

This skill is **on-demand**. It runs only when the user explicitly asks for one
of the actions documented below. It never writes to the vault on its own.

## Vault constants

```
VAULT      = /home/jhou/Documents/obsidian-nvidia
JOURNALS   = $VAULT/1-Journals/YYYY-MM-DD.md
NOTES      = $VAULT/2-Notes               # flat: every non-journal note lives here
ATTACH     = $VAULT/2-Notes/Attachments
ARCHIVE    = $VAULT/8-Archive             # archived projects, structurally untouched
BASES      = $VAULT/3-Bases                # .base files, queryable views over frontmatter
TEMPLATES  = $VAULT/9-Obsidian/Templates
SCRIPTS    = $VAULT/9-Obsidian/Scripts
```

## Schema (frontmatter)

Every note in `2-Notes/` carries a `type:` value from this 13-element enum:

| `type`     | Use                                            |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| product    | NVIDIA business unit                           |
| project    | An engineering project (e.g. Scenario Studio)  |
| feature    | A cross-type deliverable hub; vault mirror of a DFR Initiative. Sits below `project`, above `epic` |
| milestone  | Time-boxed slice of a project (`26-05`, `26-06`) |
| epic       | A Jira epic / concrete deliverable             |
| task       | A Jira ticket                                  |
| meeting    | A single meeting                               |
| design-doc | Technical proposal / spec                      |
| working-note | Personal scratch/coordination tied to active work, no Jira ticket, ephemeral |
| person     | Colleague index page                           |
| team       | Org team index page                            |
| area       | Long-lived theme (e.g. Infrastructure, NeRF)   |
| reference  | Stable knowledge / how-to / runbook            |

The `status:` value on `epic` and `task` notes uses this enum:

| Status      | Meaning                                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TODO`      | Planned, not started                                        |
| `Backlog`   | Wanted but not actively staged (lower priority than TODO)   |
| `WIP`       | Actively in progress                                        |
| `Testing`   | Implementation done, in test/QA phase                       |
| `In Review` | Code/design under review                                    |
| `Done`      | Completed and merged/shipped                                |
| `Blocked`   | Stuck on external dependency                                |
| `Cancelled` | Decided not to do                                           |
| `Archived`  | Frozen, moved to `8-Archive/` (set by `archive-note.sh`)      |

Bases that show "open work" (`Active Epics`, `Open Tasks`) use negative
filters (`status NOT IN ("Done", "Archived", "Cancelled")`), so adding new
in-flight statuses doesn't require Bases edits.

Relationships are **wikilinks in frontmatter**, not folders:

```yaml
# feature (the hub)
type: feature
project: "[[Scenario Studio]]"
jira: "https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/DFR-3169"
status: WIP

# epic
type: epic
project: "[[Scenario Studio]]"
milestone: "[[26-05]]"
jira: "https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/AVCI-1234"
status: WIP

# task
type: task
project: "[[Scenario Studio]]"
epic: "[[Fast mapping pipeline]]"
jira: "https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/AVCI-2345"
status: TODO
```

The `jira:` key is polymorphic by `type`: on an `epic` it's the Jira epic URL,
on a `task` it's the Jira ticket URL, and on a `feature` it's the DFR Initiative
URL (project `DFR` = "DriveSim 2.0 - Feature Requests"; every DFR issue is
issuetype `Initiative`). URL prefix: `https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/<KEY>`.

### Feature clusters

A `feature` groups notes that serve **one deliverable but span several `type:`
values** (a design-doc, a task, two references, a working-note…). Membership is
the `feature:` key on each CHILD, pointing at the hub:

```yaml
# any child note — keeps its OWN real type
type: design-doc
feature: "[[Controllable scene elements (lights, props) - overview]]"
```

Rules that make this work:

- Children keep their real `type:`, so they still appear in `Open Tasks`,
  `Design Docs`, `Working Notes`. Membership is orthogonal to type — this is
  what a folder could not do.
- `feature:` is the source of truth for membership. Do NOT hand-maintain a list
  of children in the hub's body; it goes stale. Let the per-feature base derive
  it, and keep prose links only as narrative ("where to start").
- `feature:` satisfies the validator's parent-link check for both `task` and
  `epic`, and is link-checked for dangling targets like every other LINK_KEY.
- The per-feature view is an INLINE ` ```base ` code block in the hub note, NOT
  a file in `3-Bases/`. `3-Bases/` is the vault-wide index namespace (every base
  there answers "all notes of type X"); a view that can only ever describe ONE
  note belongs in that note. Inline blocks take the same YAML schema as a `.base`
  file (`filters` / `properties` / `formulas` / `views` all valid).

  ````markdown
  ```base
  filters:
    and:
      - file.ext == "md"
      - feature == link(this)
  views:
    - type: table
      name: All notes in this feature
  ```
  ````

- `feature == link(this)` is the whole point. Inside an inline block `this` is
  the CONTAINING note, so the block is self-scoping: copy it into any new feature
  hub unchanged and it just works. Two things it avoids:
  - The filter MUST construct a Link. Bases is typed and does NOT coerce
    `"[[Name]]"` into a link, so a raw-string compare silently matches nothing.
  - A hardcoded `link("Some Note")` does NOT get rewritten when that note is
    renamed (Obsidian's auto-update-links does not reach into base declarations),
    so it silently breaks. `link(this)` has no name to go stale.

  Use `feature.contains(this)` instead if `feature:` is ever written as a YAML
  list rather than a single inline value.
- Combine conditions with a nested `or:` block rather than `||`. Both are valid,
  but `or:` is the form already used elsewhere in this vault.
- Precedent: `Daily Jira/MRs/Sessions.base` are global bases that self-scope via
  `this.file.basename` and are embedded in all 145 journals. Same idea — the
  difference is that a per-feature view has no vault-wide reading, so it lives
  inline instead of in `3-Bases/`.

Folder routing for `note new` is now trivial — **everything goes into
`2-Notes/`**. The user's `2-Notes/Attachments/` is also flat.

| Type       | Filename pattern                | Template file                |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| project    | `<Title>.md`                    | `Project Template.md`        |
| milestone  | `<YY-MM>.md` (e.g., `26-05.md`)   | `Milestone Template.md`      |
| epic       | `<Title>.md`                    | `Epic Template.md`           |
| task       | `<Title>.md`                    | `Task Template.md`           |
| meeting    | `<Title>.md`                    | `Meeting Note Template.md`   |
| interview  | `Interview - <Candidate>.md`    | `Interview Note.md`          |
| design-doc | `<Title>.md`                    | `Page Template.md` (no dedicated design-doc template; set `type: design-doc`) |
| person     | `<Full Name>.md`                | `People Template.md`         |
| team       | `<Team Name>.md`                | `Team Template.md`           |
| area       | `<Area Name>.md`                | `Area Template.md`           |
| reference  | `<Title>.md`                    | `Page Template.md`           |

Always confirm naming with the user when ambiguous. Filenames must be unique
within `2-Notes/` (Obsidian wikilinks resolve by stem).

## Templater placeholder rule

Vault templates contain Templater syntax (`<% tp.date.now(...) %>`,
`{{title}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{VALUE:Foo}}`). Templater only runs **inside
Obsidian**, not when omp writes the file. Therefore when this skill
materializes a template:

- Replace `<% tp.date.now("YYYY-MM-DD") %>` with today's date
- Replace `<% tp.date.now("YYYY-MM-DD", -1) %>` with yesterday's date
- Replace `{{title}}` with the note's filename stem (no extension)
- Replace `{{date}}` with today's date
- Replace `{{name}}` with the note's filename stem
- Replace `{{VALUE:Foo}}` with the value the user provides for `Foo`; if
  unknown, leave it as-is and add a `> [!todo]` callout at the top of the
  body listing every unfilled placeholder so the user can complete it
  in Obsidian.

## Commands

All commands assume `cd $VAULT` unless noted. Use the **Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep**
tools directly on the filesystem — do not shell out unless documented below.

### `note new <type> <title> [...kv]`

Create a new note from the matching template, in `2-Notes/`.

1. Validate `<type>` against the 11-element type enum above. Reject if invalid.
2. Filename: prefer human-readable `<Title>.md` (NOT kebab-case — Obsidian
   wikilinks expect human filenames, e.g., `[[Fast mapping pipeline]]`). Refuse
   if `2-Notes/<filename>` already exists.
3. Read the template, do Templater substitution per the placeholder rule.
4. For `epic`/`task`: ensure the body has a `> [!todo] Link Jira` callout for
   the user to backfill `jira:` and parent (`epic:` for tasks, `milestone:` for
   epics) if not provided as kv args.
5. Write the file. Report the absolute path.

### `find <query>`

Search the vault for `<query>`.

1. Use `Grep` with `path=/home/jhou/Documents/obsidian-nvidia`,
   `output_mode="content"`, `head_limit=30`. Exclude `.obsidian/`,
   `.git/`, `.foam/`, `2-Notes/Attachments/`.
2. If no content matches, fall back to filename glob via `Glob` over
   `**/*.md`.
3. Render results as a numbered list `<n>. <relpath>:<line>: <excerpt>`.
4. Offer to open the top hit (return the absolute path).

### `tasks open [--folder=<folder>]`

List incomplete Obsidian Tasks plugin items across the vault.

1. Use `Grep` for the regex `^\s*- \[ \] ` over `**/*.md`, scope to `<folder>`
   if given, default the whole vault excluding `.obsidian/`, `.git/`,
   `2-Notes/Attachments/`.
2. For each match, capture: file relpath, line number, the task text, and any
   trailing emoji metadata used by the Tasks plugin (`📅 YYYY-MM-DD` due,
   `⏳ YYYY-MM-DD` scheduled, `🔼/⏫/🔽/⏬` priority).
3. Group by folder. Sort within each group by due date ascending, undated
   last.
4. Render as a markdown list. Do **not** modify any file.

### `vault check [--only ERROR|WARN|INFO] [FILES...]`

Run the **read-only** vault health validator. Never modifies a note.

1. Run `python3 9-Obsidian/Scripts/validate-vault.py` (add `--only ERROR` to
   show only blocking issues, or pass specific files to scope the check).
2. The script checks, per note in `2-Notes/` (journals and the
   machine-generated `4-Activity/` notes are exempt from the type rule; the
   `obsidian-daily` skill documents the 4-Activity vocabulary):
   - **ERROR** — `type:` not in the 13-element enum; `status:` (on epic/task)
     not in the status enum; milestone filename not zero-padded `YY-MM`.
   - **WARN** — wikilink in a relationship key (`project`/`milestone`/`epic`/
     `parent`/`depends`/`team`/`area`) pointing at a note stem that doesn't
     exist (dangling/stale-PARA-path link); malformed `jira:` URL; epic/task
     with no parent link.
   - **INFO** — epic/task with no `jira:` field (widespread, advisory only).
3. Exit code is `1` if any ERROR exists, else `0` — safe for pre-commit or
   timer use.
4. Report the summary line (counts) and the ERROR/WARN findings to the user.
   **Do not auto-fix.** If the user asks to fix, use `migrate-frontmatter.py`
   (frontmatter) or `notesmd-cli move` (rename + backlink rewrite) — and
   confirm each change first.

The validator encodes **observed vault reality**, which differs from the
schema table above in two known ways: tasks link their parent via `parent:`
(a list), not `epic:`; and most epics/tasks have no `jira:` field. Those are
WARN/INFO, not ERROR, so a clean-ish vault still exits 0.

### `vault find-empty [--start <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--end <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--apply]`

Identify (and optionally delete) truly-empty daily journals — files where
nothing was hand-written AND no source activity touched the date.

1. Run `python3 9-Obsidian/Scripts/find-empty-journals.py` (default range
   `2024-01-01` → today). Without `--apply` this is a pure dry-run.
2. The classifier marks a journal **TRULY_EMPTY** iff ALL of:
   - frontmatter `type:` is `daily-note` (or absent — legacy stubs)
   - every section other than `_head`/`Notes`/`Activity (auto)`/`Summary` is
     template/placeholder (legacy `Today's Tasks`/`Today's docs` sections
     were removed 2026-06-24; the classifier still tolerates them for any
     pre-cleanup archive)
   - `Notes` body contains no real content (template lines, empty bullets,
     `tasks`/`query` plugin fences are NOT real; wikilinks, LaTeX fences,
     code fences in other langs, links, real bullet bodies ARE real)
   - no `4-Activity/*.md` has `touched_dates` containing this date
3. Files with `type:` other than `daily-note` are flagged **MISTYPED** —
   reported but NEVER auto-deleted. The user must review and either re-type
   or delete by hand.
4. Output groups TRULY_EMPTY by file size (tiny `<60b` / small `60-300b` /
   medium `300+b`); the medium bucket gets full content dumped for
   visual sanity check.
5. With `--apply`: physically `unlink()` every TRULY_EMPTY file. Always
   dry-run first; the operation is reversible only via git.

Use this AFTER any large backfill (`daily log` over a date range) to prune
stub journals that were created by the Obsidian daily-note plugin on days
the user never actually wrote anything.

### `commit [MESSAGE]`

Manual commit. Default `MESSAGE` mirrors the obsidian-git format:
`vault: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS> @ omp`.

```bash
cd $VAULT
git add -A
git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -m "<MESSAGE>"
git push origin main
```

Run via the `bash` tool. If `git diff --cached --quiet` returns zero (nothing
staged), report "nothing to commit" and skip.

#### obsidian-git auto-commit hazard (multi-step batch work)

The vault has the obsidian-git plugin with auto-commit every ~5 min, message
format `vault backup: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS> @ <hostname>`. During any multi-step
batch (reorg, bulk frontmatter rewrite, audit), the plugin will silently grab
unstaged + staged changes mid-batch and create a `vault backup: ...` commit that
may capture only PARTIAL state (renames without the in-place frontmatter rewrite,
etc.).
- Working pattern: after each batch, immediately `git add -A && git commit`. If
  an auto-commit landed mid-batch (message starts `vault backup:`), AMEND it:
  `git add -A && git commit --amend -m "<msg>"`. Don't rely on `git mv` staging
  alone — in-place frontmatter rewrites aren't staged, always `git add -A`.
- Don't push mid-batch until a known-good boundary (the plugin's auto-pull-rebase
  collides with a concurrent push — see the near-miss handling in the audit runs).
- Safety branch before a large reorg: `para-snapshot` marks a pre-reorg HEAD to
  recover from.
- obsidian-linter does NOT auto-run (all rules disabled, lintOnSave/
  lintOnFileChange false) — it only acts on explicit Cmd-P, so it is not an
  auto-mutation vector to defend against.

## Anti-patterns

- ❌ Don't expand Templater syntax in templates that are *staying* as
  templates (anything under `9-Obsidian/Templates/` or `.foam/templates/`).
  Only expand when materializing a real note.
- ❌ Don't fight `obsidian-git`. If the working tree has uncommitted changes
  from the plugin's auto-save cycle, do `git pull --rebase` before any
  vault-wide rewrite, and let the plugin's next tick push.

## Quick reference card

```
note  new <type> <title>      → new note from template, routed to PARA
find  <query>                 → grep + filename search across vault
tasks open [--folder=...]     → all open `- [ ]` tasks, grouped + sorted
vault check [--only ERROR]    → read-only health validator (type/status enum,
                                milestone padding, dangling links, jira format)
vault find-empty [--apply]    → dry-run (default) or delete truly-empty daily
                                journals (no notes, no tasks, no activity)
commit [MESSAGE]              → git add -A && commit && push (manual)
```

## Bases (`3-Bases/*.base`)

Bases is Obsidian's first-party query/database system (1.12+). The vault has
these `.base` files under `3-Bases/`:

| Base                | Filter                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `People.base`       | `type == "person"`                                        |
| `Teams.base`        | `type == "team"`                                          |
| `Products.base`     | `type == "product"`                                       |
| `Meetings.base`     | `type == "meeting"`, sorted by `date` desc                |
| `Design Docs.base`  | `type == "design-doc"`                                    |
| `Active Epics.base` | `type == "epic" AND status != "Done"`                    |
| `Open Tasks.base`   | `type == "task" AND status != "Done"`, sorted by status, date |
| `Working Notes.base`| `type == "working-note"`                                  |
| `Features.base`     | `type == "feature"` — index of every feature hub          |


Open in Obsidian to view as sortable/filterable tables. They are the canonical
"index" of the vault — folders no longer act as indexes.

## Layer 2 — `notesmd-cli` wrappers

`notesmd-cli` (formerly `Yakitrak/obsidian-cli`, renamed after Obsidian Inc
released its own CLI) is installed at `/home/jhou/.local/bin/notesmd-cli` and
the vault `obsidian-nvidia` is registered as the default. It is a Go binary
that manipulates files headlessly and uses the `obsidian://` URI scheme only
for the `open` command. Use it when an action needs the **running** Obsidian
app (focus a note, open the fuzzy search picker, follow links) or when the
filesystem-only path is more awkward than a one-liner.

The skill commands above stay primary — they go through Read/Write/Edit/Grep
because that gives full control over the substitutions and the Activity
block. `notesmd-cli` is a complement, not a replacement.

### When to prefer `notesmd-cli` over filesystem tools

| Need                                  | Use this                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Surface a note in the running GUI     | `notesmd-cli open "<path-from-vault-root>"`                |
| Open today's daily in Obsidian        | `notesmd-cli daily`                                        |
| Append a quick line to today's daily  | `notesmd-cli daily --content "<text>"` *(appends, not idempotent — do NOT use inside `daily log`)* |
| Fuzzy-pick a note interactively       | `notesmd-cli search` *(only useful when user is at the terminal)* |
| Bulk grep with JSON output for a script | `notesmd-cli search-content "<term>" --format json`      |
| Read/edit a frontmatter field         | `notesmd-cli frontmatter "<note>" --print` / `--edit --key X --value Y` |
| Rename and rewrite all backlinks      | `notesmd-cli move "<old>" "<new>"`                          |

### When NOT to use `notesmd-cli`

- ❌ Don't use it inside `daily log` — that command must be **idempotent**
  and `notesmd-cli daily --content` always appends, producing duplicates on
  re-runs. Stick with `Edit` of the `## Activity (auto)` block.
- ❌ Don't use `notesmd-cli create` for `note new` — it cannot do Templater
  substitution (the rules section above). Read the template, substitute,
  then `Write`.
- ❌ Don't shell to `notesmd-cli open` from inside a scheduled job — there
  is no running Obsidian on the timer's user-session in general; it'll
  silently no-op or pop the GUI.

### Frontmatter example

The `move` and `frontmatter` commands are the two genuine wins over raw
filesystem tools because they keep backlinks consistent and parse YAML
correctly:

```bash
# rename a project + rewrite all `[[old-name]]` and Dataview links
notesmd-cli move "2-Notes/old-name.md" "2-Notes/new-name.md"

# flip a project to in-progress without opening the file
notesmd-cli frontmatter "2-Notes/foo.md" --edit --key status --value WIP
notesmd-cli frontmatter "2-Notes/foo.md" --edit --key started --value "$(date +%F)"
```

Both run headlessly and respect the vault's existing structure.

## Layer 3 — `vault-rag-cli` semantic search

`vault-rag-cli` is a thin wrapper at `/home/jhou/.local/bin/vault-rag-cli` over
local Ollama (`bge-m3` 1024-dim embeddings) + a `sqlite-vec` index stored at
`~/.cache/vault-rag/index.db`. Use it whenever a question is **semantic**
("what did I write about X across my vault") rather than **literal** (a known
filename or exact term — those still go through `Grep`/`notesmd-cli`).

### Commands

```bash
vault-rag-cli index                              # incremental: skips files whose SHA1 is unchanged
vault-rag-cli query "<question>"     [-k 5]      # natural-language query, prints path + score + snippet
vault-rag-cli query "..." --paths-only -k 10     # just file paths, suitable for piping into Read
```

### When to prefer `vault-rag-cli` over Grep

| Need                                                              | Use this              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| "What did I write about <fuzzy concept>?"                         | `vault-rag-cli query` |
| "Find notes related to <topic> even if the keyword isn't there"   | `vault-rag-cli query` |
| "Find all files containing the literal string `customfield_10005`" | `Grep`/`notesmd-cli`  |
| "Find a note by partial filename"                                 | `Glob`/`notesmd-cli`  |

The skill commands stay primary. `vault-rag-cli` is a complement: when a user
asks a vague "what did I think about Y?", run `vault-rag-cli query "Y" -k 5`,
then `Read` the top hits before answering.

### Index hygiene

- Index lives at `~/.cache/vault-rag/index.db` (~5 MB for ~440 notes). Outside
  the vault directory, so safe from `obsidian-git` auto-commits.
- Re-indexing is **incremental**: each file is keyed by SHA1 of its content,
  so unchanged files are skipped (`vault-rag-cli index` is idempotent and
  fast — ~5 sec for an unchanged vault, ~1 sec per 50 changed files).
- Excludes `.opencode/`, `.foam/`, `8-Archive/`, `9-Obsidian/`, `node_modules/`,
  `.obsidian/`, `.smart-env/`, `.git/`. Source list: `EXCLUDE_PREFIXES` in
  `~/.local/bin/vault-rag/index.py`.
- Empty / boilerplate-only journal placeholders (`## Tasks` headers with no
  body) are intentionally **not embedded** because `bge-m3` returns NaN
  embeddings for near-empty inputs (ollama then 500s on JSON-encode).
- After bulk vault edits (mass frontmatter migration, large rename), run
  `vault-rag-cli index` once to refresh affected files.

### Anti-patterns

- ❌ Don't use it for "find the file named `Foo.md`" — it'll work but `Glob`
  is faster and exact.
- ❌ Don't expect it to find content in `8-Archive/` — archived notes are
  intentionally excluded.
- ❌ Don't embed it inside `daily log` — embedding cost is small but `daily
  log` should stay deterministic and source-of-truth-only. RAG belongs in
  interactive read paths, not the activity-block writer.

# Obsidian Vault Operations

Operate on the user's personal Obsidian vault at
`/home/jhou/Documents/obsidian-nvidia` ("the vault" hereafter). This structural
skill covers the flat `2-Notes/` note system, frontmatter schema, templates,
tasks, Bases views, search, and manual commits.

This skill is **on-demand**. It runs only when the user explicitly asks for one
of the actions documented below. It never writes to the vault on its own.

## Vault constants

```
VAULT      = /home/jhou/Documents/obsidian-nvidia
JOURNALS   = $VAULT/1-Journals/YYYY-MM-DD.md
NOTES      = $VAULT/2-Notes               # flat: every non-journal note lives here
ATTACH     = $VAULT/2-Notes/Attachments
ARCHIVE    = $VAULT/8-Archive             # archived projects, structurally untouched
BASES      = $VAULT/3-Bases                # .base files, queryable views over frontmatter
TEMPLATES  = $VAULT/9-Obsidian/Templates
SCRIPTS    = $VAULT/9-Obsidian/Scripts
```

## Schema (frontmatter)

Every note in `2-Notes/` carries a `type:` value from this 13-element enum:

| `type`     | Use                                            |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| product    | NVIDIA business unit                           |
| project    | An engineering project (e.g. Scenario Studio)  |
| feature    | A cross-type deliverable hub; vault mirror of a DFR Initiative. Sits below `project`, above `epic` |
| milestone  | Time-boxed slice of a project (`26-05`, `26-06`) |
| epic       | A Jira epic / concrete deliverable             |
| task       | A Jira ticket                                  |
| meeting    | A single meeting                               |
| design-doc | Technical proposal / spec                      |
| working-note | Personal scratch/coordination tied to active work, no Jira ticket, ephemeral |
| person     | Colleague index page                           |
| team       | Org team index page                            |
| area       | Long-lived theme (e.g. Infrastructure, NeRF)   |
| reference  | Stable knowledge / how-to / runbook            |

The `status:` value on `epic` and `task` notes uses this enum:

| Status      | Meaning                                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TODO`      | Planned, not started                                        |
| `Backlog`   | Wanted but not actively staged (lower priority than TODO)   |
| `WIP`       | Actively in progress                                        |
| `Testing`   | Implementation done, in test/QA phase                       |
| `In Review` | Code/design under review                                    |
| `Done`      | Completed and merged/shipped                                |
| `Blocked`   | Stuck on external dependency                                |
| `Cancelled` | Decided not to do                                           |
| `Archived`  | Frozen, moved to `8-Archive/` (set by `archive-note.sh`)      |

Bases that show "open work" (`Active Epics`, `Open Tasks`) use negative
filters (`status NOT IN ("Done", "Archived", "Cancelled")`), so adding new
in-flight statuses doesn't require Bases edits.

Relationships are **wikilinks in frontmatter**, not folders:

```yaml
# feature (the hub)
type: feature
project: "[[Scenario Studio]]"
jira: "https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/DFR-3169"
status: WIP

# epic
type: epic
project: "[[Scenario Studio]]"
milestone: "[[26-05]]"
jira: "https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/AVCI-1234"
status: WIP

# task
type: task
project: "[[Scenario Studio]]"
epic: "[[Fast mapping pipeline]]"
jira: "https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/AVCI-2345"

```

The `jira:` key is polymorphic by `type`: on an `epic` it's the Jira epic URL,
on a `task` it's the Jira ticket URL, and on a `feature` it's the DFR Initiative
URL (project `DFR` = "DriveSim 2.0 - Feature Requests"; every DFR issue is
issuetype `Initiative`). URL prefix: `https://jirasw.nvidia.com/browse/<KEY>`.

### Feature clusters

A `feature` groups notes that serve **one deliverable but span several `type:`
values** (a design-doc, a task, two references, a working-note…). Membership is
the `feature:` key on each CHILD, pointing at the hub:

```yaml
# any child note — keeps its OWN real type
type: design-doc
feature: "[[Controllable scene elements (lights, props) - overview]]"
```

Rules that make this work:

- Children keep their real `type:`, so they still appear in `Open Tasks`,
  `Design Docs`, `Working Notes`. Membership is orthogonal to type — this is
  what a folder could not do.
- `feature:` is the source of truth for membership. Do NOT hand-maintain a list
  of children in the hub's body; it goes stale. Let the per-feature base derive
  it, and keep prose links only as narrative ("where to start").
- `feature:` satisfies the validator's parent-link check for both `task` and
  `epic`, and is link-checked for dangling targets like every other LINK_KEY.
- The per-feature view is an INLINE ` ```base ` code block in the hub note, NOT
  a file in `3-Bases/`. `3-Bases/` is the vault-wide index namespace (every base
  there answers "all notes of type X"); a view that can only ever describe ONE
  note belongs in that note. Inline blocks take the same YAML schema as a `.base`
  file (`filters` / `properties` / `formulas` / `views` all valid).

  ````markdown
  ```base
  filters:
    and:
      - file.ext == "md"
      - feature == link(this)
  views:
    - type: table
      name: All notes in this feature
  ```
  ````

- `feature == link(this)` is the whole point. Inside an inline block `this` is
  the CONTAINING note, so the block is self-scoping: copy it into any new feature
  hub unchanged and it just works. Two things it avoids:
  - The filter MUST construct a Link. Bases is typed and does NOT coerce
    `"[[Name]]"` into a link, so a raw-string compare silently matches nothing.
  - A hardcoded `link("Some Note")` does NOT get rewritten when that note is
    renamed (Obsidian's auto-update-links does not reach into base declarations),
    so it silently breaks. `link(this)` has no name to go stale.

  Use `feature.contains(this)` instead if `feature:` is ever written as a YAML
  list rather than a single inline value.
- Combine conditions with a nested `or:` block rather than `||`. Both are valid,
  but `or:` is the form already used elsewhere in this vault.
- Precedent: `Daily Jira/MRs/Sessions.base` are global bases that self-scope via
  `this.file.basename` and are embedded in all 145 journals. Same idea — the
  difference is that a per-feature view has no vault-wide reading, so it lives
  inline instead of in `3-Bases/`.

Folder routing for `note new` is now trivial — **everything goes into
`2-Notes/`**. The user's `2-Notes/Attachments/` is also flat.

| Type       | Filename pattern                | Template file                |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| project    | `<Title>.md`                    | `Project Template.md`        |
| milestone  | `<YY-MM>.md` (e.g., `26-05.md`)   | `Milestone Template.md`      |
| epic       | `<Title>.md`                    | `Epic Template.md`           |
| task       | `<Title>.md`                    | `Task Template.md`           |
| meeting    | `<Title>.md`                    | `Meeting Note Template.md`   |
| interview  | `Interview - <Candidate>.md`    | `Interview Note.md`          |
| design-doc | `<Title>.md`                    | `Page Template.md` (no dedicated design-doc template; set `type: design-doc`) |
| person     | `<Full Name>.md`                | `People Template.md`         |
| team       | `<Team Name>.md`                | `Team Template.md`           |
| area       | `<Area Name>.md`                | `Area Template.md`           |
| reference  | `<Title>.md`                    | `Page Template.md`           |

Always confirm naming with the user when ambiguous. Filenames must be unique
within `2-Notes/` (Obsidian wikilinks resolve by stem).

## Templater placeholder rule

Vault templates contain Templater syntax (`<% tp.date.now(...) %>`,
`{{title}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{VALUE:Foo}}`). Templater only runs **inside
Obsidian**, not when omp writes the file. Therefore when this skill
materializes a template:

- Replace `<% tp.date.now("YYYY-MM-DD") %>` with today's date
- Replace `<% tp.date.now("YYYY-MM-DD", -1) %>` with yesterday's date
- Replace `{{title}}` with the note's filename stem (no extension)
- Replace `{{date}}` with today's date
- Replace `{{name}}` with the note's filename stem
- Replace `{{VALUE:Foo}}` with the value the user provides for `Foo`; if
  unknown, leave it as-is and add a `> [!todo]` callout at the top of the
  body listing every unfilled placeholder so the user can complete it
  in Obsidian.

## Commands

All commands assume `cd $VAULT` unless noted. Use the **Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep**
tools directly on the filesystem — do not shell out unless documented below.

### `note new <type> <title> [...kv]`

Create a new note from the matching template, in `2-Notes/`.

1. Validate `<type>` against the 11-element type enum above. Reject if invalid.
2. Filename: prefer human-readable `<Title>.md` (NOT kebab-case — Obsidian
   wikilinks expect human filenames, e.g., `[[Fast mapping pipeline]]`). Refuse
   if `2-Notes/<filename>` already exists.
3. Read the template, do Templater substitution per the placeholder rule.
4. For `epic`/`task`: ensure the body has a `> [!todo] Link Jira` callout for
   the user to backfill `jira:` and parent (`epic:` for tasks, `milestone:` for
   epics) if not provided as kv args.
5. Write the file. Report the absolute path.

### `find <query>`

Search the vault for `<query>`.

1. Use `Grep` with `path=/home/jhou/Documents/obsidian-nvidia`,
   `output_mode="content"`, `head_limit=30`. Exclude `.obsidian/`,
   `.git/`, `.foam/`, `2-Notes/Attachments/`.
2. If no content matches, fall back to filename glob via `Glob` over
   `**/*.md`.
3. Render results as a numbered list `<n>. <relpath>:<line>: <excerpt>`.
4. Offer to open the top hit (return the absolute path).

### `tasks open [--folder=<folder>]`

List incomplete Obsidian Tasks plugin items across the vault.

1. Use `Grep` for the regex `^\s*- \[ \] ` over `**/*.md`, scope to `<folder>`
   if given, default the whole vault excluding `.obsidian/`, `.git/`,
   `2-Notes/Attachments/`.
2. For each match, capture: file relpath, line number, the task text, and any
   trailing emoji metadata used by the Tasks plugin (`📅 YYYY-MM-DD` due,
   `⏳ YYYY-MM-DD` scheduled, `🔼/⏫/🔽/⏬` priority).
3. Group by folder. Sort within each group by due date ascending, undated
   last.
4. Render as a markdown list. Do **not** modify any file.

### `vault check [--only ERROR|WARN|INFO] [FILES...]`

Run the **read-only** vault health validator. Never modifies a note.

1. Run `python3 9-Obsidian/Scripts/validate-vault.py` (add `--only ERROR` to
   show only blocking issues, or pass specific files to scope the check).
2. The script checks, per note in `2-Notes/` (journals and the
   machine-generated `4-Activity/` notes are exempt from the type rule; the
   `obsidian-daily` skill documents the 4-Activity vocabulary):
   - **ERROR** — `type:` not in the 13-element enum; `status:` (on epic/task)
     not in the status enum; milestone filename not zero-padded `YY-MM`.
   - **WARN** — wikilink in a relationship key (`project`/`milestone`/`epic`/
     `parent`/`depends`/`team`/`area`) pointing at a note stem that doesn't
     exist (dangling/stale-PARA-path link); malformed `jira:` URL; epic/task
     with no parent link.
   - **INFO** — epic/task with no `jira:` field (widespread, advisory only).
3. Exit code is `1` if any ERROR exists, else `0` — safe for pre-commit or
   timer use.
4. Report the summary line (counts) and the ERROR/WARN findings to the user.
   **Do not auto-fix.** If the user asks to fix, use `migrate-frontmatter.py`
   (frontmatter) or `notesmd-cli move` (rename + backlink rewrite) — and
   confirm each change first.

The validator encodes **observed vault reality**, which differs from the
schema table above in two known ways: tasks link their parent via `parent:`
(a list), not `epic:`; and most epics/tasks have no `jira:` field. Those are
WARN/INFO, not ERROR, so a clean-ish vault still exits 0.

### `vault find-empty [--start <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--end <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--apply]`

Identify (and optionally delete) truly-empty daily journals — files where
nothing was hand-written AND no source activity touched the date.

1. Run `python3 9-Obsidian/Scripts/find-empty-journals.py` (default range
   `2024-01-01` → today). Without `--apply` this is a pure dry-run.
2. The classifier marks a journal **TRULY_EMPTY** iff ALL of:
   - frontmatter `type:` is `daily-note` (or absent — legacy stubs)
   - every section other than `_head`/`Notes`/`Activity (auto)`/`Summary` is
     template/placeholder (legacy `Today's Tasks`/`Today's docs` sections
     were removed 2026-06-24; the classifier still tolerates them for any
     pre-cleanup archive)
   - `Notes` body contains no real content (template lines, empty bullets,
     `tasks`/`query` plugin fences are NOT real; wikilinks, LaTeX fences,
     code fences in other langs, links, real bullet bodies ARE real)
   - no `4-Activity/*.md` has `touched_dates` containing this date
3. Files with `type:` other than `daily-note` are flagged **MISTYPED** —
   reported but NEVER auto-deleted. The user must review and either re-type
   or delete by hand.
4. Output groups TRULY_EMPTY by file size (tiny `<60b` / small `60-300b` /
   medium `300+b`); the medium bucket gets full content dumped for
   visual sanity check.
5. With `--apply`: physically `unlink()` every TRULY_EMPTY file. Always
   dry-run first; the operation is reversible only via git.

Use this AFTER any large backfill (`daily log` over a date range) to prune
stub journals that were created by the Obsidian daily-note plugin on days
the user never actually wrote anything.

### `commit [MESSAGE]`

Manual commit. Default `MESSAGE` mirrors the obsidian-git format:
`vault: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS> @ omp`.

```bash
cd $VAULT
git add -A
git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -m "<MESSAGE>"
git push origin main
```

Run via the `bash` tool. If `git diff --cached --quiet` returns zero (nothing
staged), report "nothing to commit" and skip.

#### obsidian-git auto-commit hazard (multi-step batch work)

The vault has the obsidian-git plugin with auto-commit every ~5 min, message
format `vault backup: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS> @ <hostname>`. During any multi-step
batch (reorg, bulk frontmatter rewrite, audit), the plugin will silently grab
unstaged + staged changes mid-batch and create a `vault backup: ...` commit that
may capture only PARTIAL state (renames without the in-place frontmatter rewrite,
etc.).
- Working pattern: after each batch, immediately `git add -A && git commit`. If
  an auto-commit landed mid-batch (message starts `vault backup:`), AMEND it:
  `git add -A && git commit --amend -m "<msg>"`. Don't rely on `git mv` staging
  alone — in-place frontmatter rewrites aren't staged, always `git add -A`.
- Don't push mid-batch until a known-good boundary (the plugin's auto-pull-rebase
  collides with a concurrent push — see the near-miss handling in the audit runs).
- Safety branch before a large reorg: `para-snapshot` marks a pre-reorg HEAD to
  recover from.
- obsidian-linter does NOT auto-run (all rules disabled, lintOnSave/
  lintOnFileChange false) — it only acts on explicit Cmd-P, so it is not an
  auto-mutation vector to defend against.

## Anti-patterns

- ❌ Don't expand Templater syntax in templates that are *staying* as
  templates (anything under `9-Obsidian/Templates/` or `.foam/templates/`).
  Only expand when materializing a real note.
- ❌ Don't fight `obsidian-git`. If the working tree has uncommitted changes
  from the plugin's auto-save cycle, do `git pull --rebase` before any
  vault-wide rewrite, and let the plugin's next tick push.

## Quick reference card

```
note  new <type> <title>      → new note from template, routed to PARA
find  <query>                 → grep + filename search across vault
tasks open [--folder=...]     → all open `- [ ]` tasks, grouped + sorted
vault check [--only ERROR]    → read-only health validator (type/status enum,
                                milestone padding, dangling links, jira format)
vault find-empty [--apply]    → dry-run (default) or delete truly-empty daily
                                journals (no notes, no tasks, no activity)
commit [MESSAGE]              → git add -A && commit && push (manual)
```

## Bases (`3-Bases/*.base`)

Bases is Obsidian's first-party query/database system (1.12+). The vault has
these `.base` files under `3-Bases/`:

| Base                | Filter                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `People.base`       | `type == "person"`                                        |
| `Teams.base`        | `type == "team"`                                          |
| `Products.base`     | `type == "product"`                                       |
| `Meetings.base`     | `type == "meeting"`, sorted by `date` desc                |
| `Design Docs.base`  | `type == "design-doc"`                                    |
| `Active Epics.base` | `type == "epic" AND status != "Done"`                    |
| `Open Tasks.base`   | `type == "task" AND status != "Done"`, sorted by status, date |
| `Working Notes.base`| `type == "working-note"`                                  |
| `Features.base`     | `type == "feature"` — index of every feature hub          |


Open in Obsidian to view as sortable/filterable tables. They are the canonical
"index" of the vault — folders no longer act as indexes.

## Layer 2 — `notesmd-cli` wrappers

`notesmd-cli` (formerly `Yakitrak/obsidian-cli`, renamed after Obsidian Inc
released its own CLI) is installed at `/home/jhou/.local/bin/notesmd-cli` and
the vault `obsidian-nvidia` is registered as the default. It is a Go binary
that manipulates files headlessly and uses the `obsidian://` URI scheme only
for the `open` command. Use it when an action needs the **running** Obsidian
app (focus a note, open the fuzzy search picker, follow links) or when the
filesystem-only path is more awkward than a one-liner.

The skill commands above stay primary — they go through Read/Write/Edit/Grep
because that gives full control over the substitutions and the Activity
block. `notesmd-cli` is a complement, not a replacement.

### When to prefer `notesmd-cli` over filesystem tools

| Need                                  | Use this                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Surface a note in the running GUI     | `notesmd-cli open "<path-from-vault-root>"`                |
| Open today's daily in Obsidian        | `notesmd-cli daily`                                        |
| Append a quick line to today's daily  | `notesmd-cli daily --content "<text>"` *(appends, not idempotent — do NOT use inside `daily log`)* |
| Fuzzy-pick a note interactively       | `notesmd-cli search` *(only useful when user is at the terminal)* |
| Bulk grep with JSON output for a script | `notesmd-cli search-content "<term>" --format json`      |
| Read/edit a frontmatter field         | `notesmd-cli frontmatter "<note>" --print` / `--edit --key X --value Y` |
| Rename and rewrite all backlinks      | `notesmd-cli move "<old>" "<new>"`                          |

### When NOT to use `notesmd-cli`

- ❌ Don't use it inside `daily log` — that command must be **idempotent**
  and `notesmd-cli daily --content` always appends, producing duplicates on
  re-runs. Stick with `Edit` of the `## Activity (auto)` block.
- ❌ Don't use `notesmd-cli create` for `note new` — it cannot do Templater
  substitution (the rules section above). Read the template, substitute,
  then `Write`.
- ❌ Don't shell to `notesmd-cli open` from inside a scheduled job — there
  is no running Obsidian on the timer's user-session in general; it'll
  silently no-op or pop the GUI.

### Frontmatter example

The `move` and `frontmatter` commands are the two genuine wins over raw
filesystem tools because they keep backlinks consistent and parse YAML
correctly:

```bash
# rename a project + rewrite all `[[old-name]]` and Dataview links
notesmd-cli move "2-Notes/old-name.md" "2-Notes/new-name.md"

# flip a project to in-progress without opening the file
notesmd-cli frontmatter "2-Notes/foo.md" --edit --key status --value WIP
notesmd-cli frontmatter "2-Notes/foo.md" --edit --key started --value "$(date +%F)"
```

Both run headlessly and respect the vault's existing structure.

## Layer 3 — `vault-rag-cli` semantic search

`vault-rag-cli` is a thin wrapper at `/home/jhou/.local/bin/vault-rag-cli` over
local Ollama (`bge-m3` 1024-dim embeddings) + a `sqlite-vec` index stored at
`~/.cache/vault-rag/index.db`. Use it whenever a question is **semantic**
("what did I write about X across my vault") rather than **literal** (a known
filename or exact term — those still go through `Grep`/`notesmd-cli`).

### Commands

```bash
vault-rag-cli index                              # incremental: skips files whose SHA1 is unchanged
vault-rag-cli query "<question>"     [-k 5]      # natural-language query, prints path + score + snippet
vault-rag-cli query "..." --paths-only -k 10     # just file paths, suitable for piping into Read
```

### When to prefer `vault-rag-cli` over Grep

| Need                                                              | Use this              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| "What did I write about <fuzzy concept>?"                         | `vault-rag-cli query` |
| "Find notes related to <topic> even if the keyword isn't there"   | `vault-rag-cli query` |
| "Find all files containing the literal string `customfield_10005`" | `Grep`/`notesmd-cli`  |
| "Find a note by partial filename"                                 | `Glob`/`notesmd-cli`  |

The skill commands stay primary. `vault-rag-cli` is a complement: when a user
asks a vague "what did I think about Y?", run `vault-rag-cli query "Y" -k 5`,
then `Read` the top hits before answering.

### Index hygiene

- Index lives at `~/.cache/vault-rag/index.db` (~5 MB for ~440 notes). Outside
  the vault directory, so safe from `obsidian-git` auto-commits.
- Re-indexing is **incremental**: each file is keyed by SHA1 of its content,
  so unchanged files are skipped (`vault-rag-cli index` is idempotent and
  fast — ~5 sec for an unchanged vault, ~1 sec per 50 changed files).
- Excludes `.opencode/`, `.foam/`, `8-Archive/`, `9-Obsidian/`, `node_modules/`,
  `.obsidian/`, `.smart-env/`, `.git/`. Source list: `EXCLUDE_PREFIXES` in
  `~/.local/bin/vault-rag/index.py`.
- Empty / boilerplate-only journal placeholders (`## Tasks` headers with no
  body) are intentionally **not embedded** because `bge-m3` returns NaN
  embeddings for near-empty inputs (ollama then 500s on JSON-encode).
- After bulk vault edits (mass frontmatter migration, large rename), run
  `vault-rag-cli index` once to refresh affected files.

### Anti-patterns

- ❌ Don't use it for "find the file named `Foo.md`" — it'll work but `Glob`
  is faster and exact.
- ❌ Don't expect it to find content in `8-Archive/` — archived notes are
  intentionally excluded.
- ❌ Don't embed it inside `daily log` — embedding cost is small but `daily
  log` should stay deterministic and source-of-truth-only. RAG belongs in
  interactive read paths, not the activity-block writer.

# Heeler fork — iOS herdr client build plan

Personal iOS client for supervising omp agents running in herdr on the devbox, built by **forking Heeler** (Apache-2.0). I do not write the code — agents code, I review design/architecture/implementation. Build target: my MacBook + free Apple ID (weekly rebuild, no $99 dev account).

**Decision record**: Fork Heeler, not Drover. Drover (MIT, Flutter) has the omp chat parser but a CLI-over-SSH transport I reject, and its transport rewrite is foundational/risky. Heeler has the socket-API transport, event stream, sessions, workspaces, pairing, jump hosts, SFTP all done — the one big gap (chat view) is additive and has a reference implementation to port. Full comparison rationale below.

## Requirements

1. **Chat view for agent history** — omp first (native JSONL transcripts), other agents better too
2. **Minimal chrome** — maximal chat area, minimal other UI
3. **Detail levels** — overview by default; thinking/edit/diff/toolcall hidden entirely at L0
4. **Blended hosts/sessions/workspaces** — all agents across all of them in one view
5. **Keyboard enhancement** — beyond the existing key row
6. **Input integration** — `/` slash, `#` hash, `@` mention, `!` bash, more
7. **URI/file opener** — URL in embedded/external browser; markdown in internal/external viewer; editor support; remote→local transfer silent
8. **Notifications while backgrounded/closed** — solved OUTSIDE the fork (see below)

## Constraint: free Apple ID = no APNs on the fork

Free personal-team signing **cannot get the `aps-environment` entitlement** — Apple doesn't issue push to personal teams. So the fork will never push on its own, regardless of base.

**Solution: keep upstream Heeler (TestFlight) installed as the notification surface.** Its host plugin is ALREADY installed on the devbox (v0.4.0, `~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/heeler`), its E2E-encrypted push works today, and it coexists with the fork (two binaries, two Device Keys, same host). The fork is the interactive app; upstream Heeler delivers blocked/done alerts. If that ever becomes annoying: Bark app + self-hosted bark-server on the devbox + forked notify plugin (~50 LOC change), but two-Heeler is zero-work.

Fork signing also means: **bundle ID must change** (can't be `dev.bybee.heeler`) and builds expire in 7 days → weekly rebuild ritual.

## Weekly build ritual (MacBook, USB iPhone)

```bash
cd heeler-fork
make install          # repo-provided target: builds Debug + installs to the
                      # first physical iPhone found via devicectl
```

One-time setup:
- Xcode → fork project → Signing & Capabilities → select my Personal Team → let Xcode fix the profile
- Change bundle ID from `dev.bybee.heeler` to something personal
- `make resolve` if SPM packages need fetching
- Rebuild **before day 7** (app dies mid-flight otherwise); pick a fixed weekday

Note: `make testflight` / `make publish` targets exist but are useless for us (no paid account). `make test` runs the 155-file test suite — agents should run it before every install.

## Heeler architecture (what to review against)

Codebase: 180 Swift files, 42.9k LOC app + 3.4k host plugin (Node) + 1.3k push relay (Cloudflare Workers). 155 test files. Repo: https://github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler — clone locally before starting.

Module map (LOC) — only **bold** modules get modified/added:

| Module | LOC | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Sources/Heeler/Transport/` | 7.5k | libssh2 direct-streamlocal onto `herdr.sock`; 18 socket-API methods; events channel; jump hosts. **extend only** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Console/` | 15k | pane-text Monitor UI. **the screen we replace/supplement with chat** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Terminal/` | 6.3k | libghostty renderer, Attach PTY. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Pairing/` | 1.2k | QR pairing. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Notifications/` + `LiveActivities/` | 3k | E2E APNs push. untouched (fork can't push anyway) |
| `Sources/Heeler/Files/`, `Attachments/` | 0.8k | SFTP staging. **extend for file openers** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Skills/`, `Snippets/` | 1.9k | herdr skills + snippets. **hook composer modes into these** |
| **new** `Chat/` | ~2-3k (est.) | transcript models + parser + chat renderer (ported from Drover) |

Key architecture facts (from ADRs — agents must read these before touching Transport):
- **ADR-0011**: one direct-streamlocal channel per RPC (herdr Unix API = one request per connection); long-lived reserved Events channel; 8+1 channel budget under OpenSSH `MaxSessions 10`
- **ADR-0012**: herdr API reality — `pane.read` capped at 1000 lines, no offsets, no replay on `events.subscribe`; `pane.agent_status_changed` is the push signal. THIS is why Heeler has no chat: pane text was the only history source it knew. Our chat layer bypasses this via SFTP + session JSONL (below)
- **ADR-0013**: Composer delivers via single `agent.prompt` (no `wait`); when agent is Blocked, insert-without-Enter into the Attach PTY instead
- **ADR-0015/0016**: shell terminals via `tab.create` + `herdr terminal attach --takeover`; Direct Input is opt-in
- `Host` model pins one `sessionName` (blank = default session); `listSessions()` already exists → **blending = N Host entries**, zero code

## Implementation plan (sequenced)

### Phase 0 — toolchain proof (before any code)
Clone fork → change bundle ID → `make install` unmodified → connect to devbox.
Pairing: `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` on devbox, scan QR from the fork. Proves signing + SSH + socket transport work end-to-end. **Do not proceed to Phase 1 until this works.**

### Phase 1 — chat layer (the big one) — 2 weeks
Port Drover's transcript stack (MIT, reference: https://github.com/keinstn/drover):

**What to port** (Drover → Heeler mapping):
- `app/lib/src/transcript/native_transcript.dart` → Swift transcript models + `JsonlTranscriptWindow` (512KiB bounded tail, append-only poll, loadOlder paging). **Increase the window constant** — devbox conversations run 1.2MB+, 512KiB initial window shows only recent history
- `app/lib/src/agents/pi/pi_transcript.dart` → Swift JSONL parser (omp reuses pi's record shapes; documented in Drover's `docs/agents/omp-notes.md`)
- Fetch path: `agent.list` already returns `agent_session: {kind:'path', value:'~/.omp/...jsonl'}` over the socket API (verified live) → new `Transport.readTranscriptFile(path)` via existing SFTP
- Parser output models: `TranscriptMessage / Thinking / ToolUse / ToolResult` (Drover's shape — keep it, it maps to omp's record types)

**omp JSONL record spec** (verified against live devbox session files — use these as test fixtures):
```
type:'message'  message.role ∈ user|assistant|toolResult|bashExecution
               content blocks: {type:'text'} {type:'thinking'} {type:'toolCall', id, name, arguments}
               NB: toolCall.arguments is already-decoded JSON — do NOT re-decode
toolResult:     own top-level record, paired by toolCallId (long, contains '|')
skip records:   top-level type ∉ {message} — title, title_change, custom_message, custom
               (customType: tool_execution_start, session_exit), thinking_level_change etc.
session files:  ~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slugified-cwd>/<ISO-ts>_<uuid>.jsonl
```
Fixture source: the live devbox sessions under `~/.omp/agent/sessions/` — real 1.2MB conversation to test parser + windowing + paging against. **Critical**: the parser must be tested against these real files, not synthetic fixtures (synthetic-fixture rule).

**New `ChatScreen`** replacing Console-per-agent detail — design requirements:
- Detail levels **designed in from the start**:
  - L0 (default): assistant `text` turns only. NO thinking, NO toolcall, NO diff, NO edit, NO spinner
  - L1: + toolcall names (one line each, collapsed)
  - L2: + tool results (collapsed, tap to expand), diffs
  - L3: + thinking blocks (collapsed)
  - Level switcher: persistent small control, not a modal
- Minimal chrome: status bar reduced to a thin strip (agent name + state + workspace/host badge); everything else full-bleed chat
- Live terminal section stays (Heeler's Attach) but demoted: collapsed-by-default strip at bottom, expand on tap — it covers the gap between "last jsonl record" and "screen now"
- Per-agent detail-level memory (persist per pane id)

### Phase 2 — sessions/hosts blending polish — days
Console already blends Hosts; each session = a Host entry. Add UX only:
- Host badge compact display (`devbox:main` style)
- Session picker in Host edit (listSessions already exists)
- Optional: auto-discover all running sessions on a host at connect → offer to add each as a Host

### Phase 3 — composer input modes — 1 week
Heeler's Composer (one-shot `agent.prompt`, Blocked-state PTY insert) is the primitive. Add a tokenizer/router in front:
- `/` → slash commands: `omp` slash commands + client-local ones (`/level 2`, `/follow <agent>`)
- `#` → tag/search: `#<workspace>`, `#<status:blocked>`, `#<agent>` — filters the blended console
- `@` → mention: `@<agent>` routes the message to that pane's `agent.prompt` (cross-host: resolve agent → host → transport)
- `!` → bash: runs via `pane run` in a scratch shell (or the agent's pane with a toggle); output inline at L1 detail, streamed
- Snippets/Skills already exist — wire `#` and Skills suggestions into the same suggestion row

### Phase 4 — URI/file openers — 1 week
Primitives exist: SFTP `stageFile/stageImage/readSkillFile`. Add:
- URL detection in chat text + terminal → open embedded (SFSafariViewController) or external (default browser) — per-domain setting
- Markdown file path in chat → fetch over SFTP silently → internal viewer (SwiftUI + swift-markdown or similar)
- "Open in editor": SFTP download → temp local file → `UIDocumentPickerViewController`/share to external editor → watch for change → silent SFTP push back. Start with download+push; the live-sync loop is v2 if clunky
- All remote→local transfers silent (no progress dialogs under ~10MB)

### Phase 5 — keyboard enhancement — days
Existing: tools keyboard (Esc/Tab/arrows/Enter), full terminal keyboard, Snippets. Add:
- Long-press chord layer (hold a key → radial menu of variants)
- Per-agent macro keys (map a key to a Snippet with args)
- Swipe on the key row = prefix key (ctrl+b) + gesture → common herdr nav

## What NOT to build (decided)

- **No push in the fork** — free Apple ID can't. Upstream TestFlight Heeler covers it (already installed + paired on the devbox side)
- **No transport rewrite** — Heeler's is the reason we chose this base
- **No Drover UI port** — the Flutter Material look is what we're escaping
- **No Firebase anything** — Drover's path only; we keep zero Google in the loop

## Review checklist (for me, when agents bring code)

1. Transport additions must respect the 8+1 channel budget (ADR-0011) — flag any per-poll channel churn
2. Parser changes tested against real devbox jsonls (1.2MB file), not fixtures
3. L0 default must render zero toolcall/thinking/diff/edit chrome — verify on the wA:p7 long-running agent conversation
4. New modules only (Chat/, composer router) — anything touching Transport/ or Terminal/ gets extra scrutiny
5. `make test` green before every weekly install
6. Upstream merges: rebase weekly from ZingerLittleBee/Heeler main — our changes are layered, merges should be near-free; if a merge touches Chat/, re-read their ADR diff first
7. License: keep NOTICE + Apache-2.0 headers; ported Drover parser code carries MIT attribution comment

## Open questions (resolve during Phase 0/1)

- [ ] dartssh2-style streamlocal in the fork is irrelevant (Heeler uses libssh2 already) — but verify the fork builds with the pinned XCFrameworks without paid account (they're checked in, should be fine)
- [ ] Decide L0 for *blocked* agents: does a pending `ask`/permission prompt force L2 detail for that turn? (probably yes — prompt visibility beats minimalism)
- [ ] omp `ask` tool dialogs are arrow-key, not numbered — the chat layer should render pending `ask` as tappable options (Drover hasn't done this; it's our chance to beat upstream on it)
- [ ] Should `!` bash mode get its own scratch pane or reuse the agent's pane? (scratch pane safer; agent pane faster to reach)

## Reference material

- Heeler repo + ADRs: https://github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler (`docs/adr/`, `CONTEXT.md`, `plugin/README.md`)
- Drover parser reference: https://github.com/keinstn/drover (`app/lib/src/transcript/`, `app/lib/src/agents/pi/`, `docs/agents/omp-notes.md` — the omp record spec)
- Drover upstream may evolve the parser (ships weekly) — pin a commit when porting, note it here
- Heeler TestFlight (notification surface): https://testflight.apple.com/join/aXSxRn4r
- herdr docs: https://herdr.dev/llms.txt — socket API + integrations
- Live fixtures on devbox: `~/.omp/agent/sessions/*/` (real omp jsonls); `herdr api snapshot --json` shapes

## Devbox host-side state (already done, for reference)

- herdr 0.9.0, default session is THE session (all agents migrated there 2026-09-13)
- omp integration installed: `herdr integration install omp` → `~/.omp/agent/extensions/herdr-omp-agent-state.ts` — **only fires at agent start**; agents started before install have no `agent_session` (bounce to register: ctrl+c + `omp --resume <jsonl>`)
- Heeler plugin installed + paired candidate: `herdr plugin list` shows heeler v0.4.0; pairing QR via `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` (2-min single-use window — invoke on demand)
- Drover also installed on the phone (PEM key auth, `~/.ssh/drover_devbox` entry in authorized_keys) — coexists; its omp chat works today

59:| Module | LOC | Role |
60:|---|---|---|
61:| `Sources/Heeler/Transport/` | 7.5k | libssh2 direct-streamlocal onto `herdr.sock`; 18 socket-API methods; events channel; jump hosts. **extend only** |

78:

80:Clone fork → change bundle ID → `make install` unmodified → connect to devbox.

95:               content blocks: {type:'text'} {type:'thinking'} {type:'toolCall', id, name, arguments}

97:toolResult:     own top-level record, paired by toolCallId (long, contains '|')
98:skip records:   top-level type ∉ {message} — title, title_change, custom_message, custom
99:               (customType: tool_execution_start, session_exit), thinking_level_change etc.
100:session files:  ~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slugified-cwd>/<ISO-ts>_<uuid>.jsonl
101:```
102:Fixture source: the live devbox sessions under `~/.omp/agent/sessions/` — real 1.2MB conversation to test parser + windowing + paging against. **Critical**: the parser must be tested against these real files, not synthetic fixtures (synthetic-fixture rule).

104:**New `ChatScreen`** replacing Console-per-agent detail — design requirements:
105:- Detail levels **designed in from the start**:
106:  - L0 (default): assistant `text` turns only. NO thinking, NO toolcall, NO diff, NO edit, NO spinner
107:  - L1: + toolcall names (one line each, collapsed)
108:  - L2: + tool results (collapsed, tap to expand), diffs
109:  - L3: + thinking blocks (collapsed)
110:  - Level switcher: persistent small control, not a modal
111:- Minimal chrome: status bar reduced to a thin strip (agent name + state + workspace/host badge); everything else full-bleed chat
112:- Live terminal section stays (Heeler's Attach) but demoted: collapsed-by-default strip at bottom, expand on tap — it covers the gap between "last jsonl record" and "screen now"

116:Heeler's Composer (one-shot `agent.prompt`, Blocked-state PTY insert) is the primitive. Add a tokenizer/router in front:
117:- `/` → slash commands: `omp` slash commands + client-local ones (`/level 2`, `/follow <agent>`)
118:- `#` → tag/search: `#<workspace>`, `#<status:blocked>`, `#<agent>` — filters the blended console
119:- `@` → mention: `@<agent>` routes the message to that pane's `agent.prompt` (cross-host: resolve agent → host → transport)
120:- `!` → bash: runs via `pane run` in a scratch shell (or the agent's pane with a toggle); output inline at L1 detail, streamed
121:- Snippets/Skills already exist — wire `#` and Skills suggestions into the same suggestion row
122:
123:### Phase 5 — keyboard enhancement — days
124:Existing: tools keyboard (Esc/Tab/arrows/Enter), full terminal keyboard, Snippets. Add:
125:- Long-press chord layer (hold a key → radial menu of variants)
126:- Per-agent macro keys (map a key to a Snippet with args)
127:- Swipe on the key row = prefix key (ctrl+b) + gesture → common herdr nav
128:
129:### Phase 4 — URI/file openers — 1 week
130:Primitives exist: SFTP `stageFile/stageImage/readSkillFile`. Add:
131:- URL detection in chat text + terminal → open embedded (SFSafariViewController) or external (default browser) — per-domain setting
132:- Markdown file path in chat → fetch over SFTP silently → internal viewer (SwiftUI + swift-markdown or similar)
133:- "Open in editor": SFTP download → temp local file → `UIDocumentPickerViewController`/share to external editor → watch for change → silent SFTP push back. Start with download+push; the live-sync loop is v2 if clunky
134:- All remote→local transfers silent (no progress dialogs under ~10MB)
135:
136:### Phase 2 — sessions/hosts blending polish — days
137:Console already blends Hosts; each session = a Host entry. Add UX only:
138:- Host badge compact display (`devbox:main` style)
139:- Session picker in Host edit (listSessions already exists)
140:- Optional: auto-discover all running sessions on a host at connect → offer to add each as a Host
141:
142:## What NOT to build (decided)
143:
144:- **No push in the fork** — free Apple ID can't. Upstream TestFlight Heeler covers it (already installed + paired on the devbox side)
145:- **No transport rewrite** — Heeler's is the reason we chose this base
146:- **No Drover UI port** — the Flutter Material look is what we're escaping
147:- **No Firebase anything** — Drover's path only; we keep zero Google in the loop
148:
149:## Review checklist (for me, when agents bring code)
150:
151:1. Transport additions must respect the 8+1 channel budget (ADR-0011) — flag any per-poll channel churn
152:2. Parser changes tested against real devbox jsonls (1.2MB file), not fixtures
153:3. L0 default must render zero toolcall/thinking/diff/edit chrome — verify on the wA:p7 long-running agent conversation
154:4. New modules only (Chat/, composer router) — anything touching Transport/ or Terminal/ gets extra scrutiny
155:5. `make test` green before every weekly install
156:6. Upstream merges: rebase weekly from ZingerLittleBee/Heeler main — our changes are layered, merges should be near-free; if a merge touches Chat/, re-read their ADR diff first
157:7. License: keep NOTICE + Apache-2.0 headers; ported Drover parser code carries MIT attribution comment
158:
159:## Open questions (resolve during Phase 0/1)
160:
161:- [ ] dartssh2-style streamlocal in the fork is irrelevant (Heeler uses libssh2 already) — but verify the fork builds with the pinned XCFrameworks without paid account (they're checked in, should be fine)
162:- [ ] Decide L0 for *blocked* agents: does a pending `ask`/permission prompt force L2 detail for that turn? (probably yes — prompt visibility beats minimalism)
163:- [ ] omp `ask` tool dialogs are arrow-key, not numbered — the chat layer should render pending `ask` as tappable options (Drover hasn't done this; it's our chance to beat upstream on it)
164:- [ ] Should `!` bash mode get its own scratch pane or reuse the agent's pane? (scratch pane safer; agent pane faster to reach)
165:
166:## Reference material
167:
168:- Heeler repo + ADRs: https://github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler (`docs/adr/`, `CONTEXT.md`, `plugin/README.md`)
169:- Drover parser reference: https://github.com/keinstn/drover (`app/lib/src/transcript/`, `app/lib/src/agents/pi/`, `docs/agents/omp-notes.md` — the omp record spec)
170:- Drover upstream may evolve the parser (ships weekly) — pin a commit when porting, note it here
171:- Heeler TestFlight (notification surface): https://testflight.apple.com/join/aXSxRn4r
172:- herdr docs: https://herdr.dev/llms.txt — socket API + integrations
173:- Live fixtures on devbox: `~/.omp/agent/sessions/*/` (real omp jsonls); `herdr api snapshot --json` shapes
174:
175:## Devbox host-side state (already done, for reference)
176:
177:- herdr 0.9.0, default session is THE session (all agents migrated there 2026-09-13)
178:- omp integration installed: `herdr integration install omp` → `~/.omp/agent/extensions/herdr-omp-agent-state.ts` — **only fires at agent start**; agents started before install have no `agent_session` (bounce to register: ctrl+c + `omp --resume <jsonl>`)
179:- Heeler plugin installed + paired candidate: `herdr plugin list` shows heeler v0.4.0; pairing QR via `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` (2-min single-use window — invoke on demand)
180:- Drover also installed on the phone (PEM key auth, `~/.ssh/drover_devbox` entry in authorized_keys) — coexists; its omp chat works today
