# Heeler fork — iOS herdr client build plan

Personal iOS client for supervising omp agents running in herdr on the devbox, built by **forking Heeler** (Apache-2.0). I do not write the code — agents code, I review design/architecture/implementation. Build target: my MacBook + free Apple ID (weekly rebuild, no $99 dev account).

**Decision record**: Fork Heeler, not Drover. Drover (MIT, Flutter) has the omp chat parser but a CLI-over-SSH transport I reject, and its transport rewrite is foundational/risky. Heeler has the socket-API transport, event stream, sessions, workspaces, pairing, jump hosts, SFTP all done — the one big gap (chat view) is additive and has a reference implementation to port. Full comparison rationale below.

## Requirements

1. **Chat view for agent history** — omp first (native JSONL transcripts), other agents better too
2. **Minimal chrome** — maximal chat area, minimal other UI
3. **Detail levels** — overview by default; thinking/edit/diff/toolcall hidden entirely at L0
4. **Blended hosts/sessions/workspaces** — all agents across all of them in one view
5. **Keyboard enhancement** — beyond the existing key row
6. **Input integration** — `/` slash, `#` hash, `@` mention, `!` bash, more
7. **URI/file opener** — URL in embedded/external browser; markdown in internal/external viewer; editor support; remote→local transfer silent
8. **Notifications while backgrounded/closed** — solved OUTSIDE the fork (see below)

## Constraint: free Apple ID = no APNs on the fork

Free personal-team signing **cannot get the `aps-environment` entitlement** — Apple doesn't issue push to personal teams. So the fork will never push on its own, regardless of base.

**Solution: keep upstream Heeler (TestFlight) installed as the notification surface.** Its host plugin is ALREADY installed on the devbox (v0.4.0, `~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/heeler`), its E2E-encrypted push works today, and it coexists with the fork (two binaries, two Device Keys, same host). The fork is the interactive app; upstream Heeler delivers blocked/done alerts. If that ever becomes annoying: Bark app + self-hosted bark-server on the devbox + forked notify plugin (~50 LOC change), but two-Heeler is zero-work.

Fork signing also means: **bundle ID must change** (can't be `dev.bybee.heeler`) and builds expire in 7 days → weekly rebuild ritual.

## Weekly build ritual (MacBook, USB iPhone)

```bash
cd heeler-fork
make install          # repo-provided target: builds Debug + installs to the
                      # first physical iPhone found via devicectl
```

One-time setup:
- Xcode → fork project → Signing & Capabilities → select my Personal Team → let Xcode fix the profile
- Change bundle ID from `dev.bybee.heeler` to something personal
- `make resolve` if SPM packages need fetching
- Rebuild **before day 7** (app dies mid-flight otherwise); pick a fixed weekday

Note: `make testflight` / `make publish` targets exist but are useless for us (no paid account). `make test` runs the 155-file test suite — agents should run it before every install.

## Heeler architecture (what to review against)

Codebase: 180 Swift files, 42.9k LOC app + 3.4k host plugin (Node) + 1.3k push relay (Cloudflare Workers). 155 test files. Repo: https://github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler — clone locally before starting.

Module map (LOC) — only **bold** modules get modified/added:

| Module | LOC | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Sources/Heeler/Transport/` | 7.5k | libssh2 direct-streamlocal onto `herdr.sock`; 18 socket-API methods; events channel; jump hosts. **extend only** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Console/` | 15k | pane-text Monitor UI. **the screen we replace/supplement with chat** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Terminal/` | 6.3k | libghostty renderer, Attach PTY. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Pairing/` | 1.2k | QR pairing. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Notifications/` + `LiveActivities/` | 3k | E2E APNs push. untouched (fork can't push anyway) |
| `Sources/Heeler/Files/`, `Attachments/` | 0.8k | SFTP staging. **extend for file openers** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Skills/`, `Snippets/` | 1.9k | herdr skills + snippets. **hook composer modes into these** |
| **new** `Chat/` | ~2-3k (est.) | transcript models + parser + chat renderer (ported from Drover) |

Key architecture facts (from ADRs — agents must read these before touching Transport):
- **ADR-0011**: one direct-streamlocal channel per RPC (herdr Unix API = one request per connection); long-lived reserved Events channel; 8+1 channel budget under OpenSSH `MaxSessions 10`
- **ADR-0012**: herdr API reality — `pane.read` capped at 1000 lines, no offsets, no replay on `events.subscribe`; `pane.agent_status_changed` is the push signal. THIS is why Heeler has no chat: pane text was the only history source it knew. Our chat layer bypasses this via SFTP + session JSONL (below)
- **ADR-0013**: Composer delivers via single `agent.prompt` (no `wait`); when agent is Blocked, insert-without-Enter into the Attach PTY instead
- **ADR-0015/0016**: shell terminals via `tab.create` + `herdr terminal attach --takeover`; Direct Input is opt-in
- `Host` model pins one `sessionName` (blank = default session); `listSessions()` already exists → **blending = N Host entries**, zero code

## Implementation plan (sequenced)

### Phase 0 — toolchain proof (before any code)
Clone fork → change bundle ID → `make install` unmodified → connect to devbox.
Pairing: `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` on devbox, scan QR from the fork. Proves signing + SSH + socket transport work end-to-end. **Do not proceed to Phase 1 until this works.**

### Phase 1 — chat layer (the big one) — 2 weeks

**What to port** (Drover → Heeler mapping):
- `app/lib/src/transcript/native_transcript.dart` → Swift transcript models + `JsonlTranscriptWindow` (512KiB bounded tail, append-only poll, loadOlder paging). **Increase the window constant** — devbox conversations run 1.2MB+, 512KiB initial window shows only recent history
- `app/lib/src/agents/pi/pi_transcript.dart` → Swift JSONL parser (omp reuses pi's record shapes; documented in Drover's `docs/agents/omp-notes.md`)

- Parser output models: `TranscriptMessage / Thinking / ToolUse / ToolResult` (Drover's shape — keep it, it maps to omp's record types)

**omp JSONL record spec** (verified against live devbox session files — use these as test fixtures):
```

**New `ChatScreen`** replacing Console-per-agent detail — design requirements:
- Detail levels **designed in from the start**:
  - L0 (default): assistant `text` turns only. NO thinking, NO toolcall, NO diff, NO edit, NO spinner
  - L1: + toolcall names (one line each, collapsed)
  - L2: + tool results (collapsed, tap to expand), diffs
  - L3: + thinking blocks (collapsed)
  - Level switcher: persistent small control, not a modal
- Minimal chrome: status bar reduced to a thin strip (agent name + state + workspace/host badge); everything else full-bleed chat
- Live terminal section stays (Heeler's Attach) but demoted: collapsed-by-default strip at bottom, expand on tap — it covers the gap between "last jsonl record" and "screen now"
- Per-agent detail-level memory (persist per pane id)

### Phase 3 — composer input modes — 1 week
Heeler's Composer (one-shot `agent.prompt`, Blocked-state PTY insert) is the primitive. Add a tokenizer/router in front:
- `/` → slash commands: `omp` slash commands + client-local ones (`/level 2`, `/follow <agent>`)

# Heeler fork — iOS herdr client build plan

Personal iOS client for supervising omp agents running in herdr on the devbox, built by **forking Heeler** (Apache-2.0). I do not write the code — agents code, I review design/architecture/implementation. Build target: my MacBook + free Apple ID (weekly rebuild, no $99 dev account).

**Decision record**: Fork Heeler, not Drover. Drover (MIT, Flutter) has the omp chat parser but a CLI-over-SSH transport I reject, and its transport rewrite is foundational/risky. Heeler has the socket-API transport, event stream, sessions, workspaces, pairing, jump hosts, SFTP all done — the one big gap (chat view) is additive and has a reference implementation to port. Full comparison rationale below.

## Requirements

1. **Chat view for agent history** — omp first (native JSONL transcripts), other agents better too
2. **Minimal chrome** — maximal chat area, minimal other UI
3. **Detail levels** — overview by default; thinking/edit/diff/toolcall hidden entirely at L0
4. **Blended hosts/sessions/workspaces** — all agents across all of them in one view
5. **Keyboard enhancement** — beyond the existing key row
6. **Input integration** — `/` slash, `#` hash, `@` mention, `!` bash, more
7. **URI/file opener** — URL in embedded/external browser; markdown in internal/external viewer; editor support; remote→local transfer silent
8. **Notifications while backgrounded/closed** — solved OUTSIDE the fork (see below)

## Constraint: free Apple ID = no APNs on the fork

Free personal-team signing **cannot get the `aps-environment` entitlement** — Apple doesn't issue push to personal teams. So the fork will never push on its own, regardless of base.

**Solution: keep upstream Heeler (TestFlight) installed as the notification surface.** Its host plugin is ALREADY installed on the devbox (v0.4.0, `~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/heeler`), its E2E-encrypted push works today, and it coexists with the fork (two binaries, two Device Keys, same host). The fork is the interactive app; upstream Heeler delivers blocked/done alerts. If that ever becomes annoying: Bark app + self-hosted bark-server on the devbox + forked notify plugin (~50 LOC change), but two-Heeler is zero-work.

Fork signing also means: **bundle ID must change** (can't be `dev.bybee.heeler`) and builds expire in 7 days → weekly rebuild ritual.

## Weekly build ritual (MacBook, USB iPhone)

```bash
cd heeler-fork
make install          # repo-provided target: builds Debug + installs to the
                      # first physical iPhone found via devicectl
```

One-time setup:
- Xcode → fork project → Signing & Capabilities → select my Personal Team → let Xcode fix the profile
- Change bundle ID from `dev.bybee.heeler` to something personal
- `make resolve` if SPM packages need fetching
- Rebuild **before day 7** (app dies mid-flight otherwise); pick a fixed weekday

Note: `make testflight` / `make publish` targets exist but are useless for us (no paid account). `make test` runs the 155-file test suite — agents should run it before every install.

## Heeler architecture (what to review against)

Codebase: 180 Swift files, 42.9k LOC app + 3.4k host plugin (Node) + 1.3k push relay (Cloudflare Workers). 155 test files. Repo: https://github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler — clone locally before starting.

Module map (LOC) — only **bold** modules get modified/added:

| Module | LOC | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Sources/Heeler/Transport/` | 7.5k | libssh2 direct-streamlocal onto `herdr.sock`; 18 socket-API methods; events channel; jump hosts. **extend only** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Console/` | 15k | pane-text Monitor UI. **the screen we replace/supplement with chat** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Terminal/` | 6.3k | libghostty renderer, Attach PTY. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Pairing/` | 1.2k | QR pairing. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Notifications/` + `LiveActivities/` | 3k | E2E APNs push. untouched (fork can't push anyway) |
| `Sources/Heeler/Files/`, `Attachments/` | 0.8k | SFTP staging. **extend for file openers** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Skills/`, `Snippets/` | 1.9k | herdr skills + snippets. **hook composer modes into these** |
| **new** `Chat/` | ~2-3k (est.) | transcript models + parser + chat renderer (ported from Drover) |

Key architecture facts (from ADRs — agents must read these before touching Transport):
- **ADR-0011**: one direct-streamlocal channel per RPC (herdr Unix API = one request per connection); long-lived reserved Events channel; 8+1 channel budget under OpenSSH `MaxSessions 10`
- **ADR-0012**: herdr API reality — `pane.read` capped at 1000 lines, no offsets, no replay on `events.subscribe`; `pane.agent_status_changed` is the push signal. THIS is why Heeler has no chat: pane text was the only history source it knew. Our chat layer bypasses this via SFTP + session JSONL (below)
- **ADR-0013**: Composer delivers via single `agent.prompt` (no `wait`); when agent is Blocked, insert-without-Enter into the Attach PTY instead
- **ADR-0015/0016**: shell terminals via `tab.create` + `herdr terminal attach --takeover`; Direct Input is opt-in
- `Host` model pins one `sessionName` (blank = default session); `listSessions()` already exists → **blending = N Host entries**, zero code

## Implementation plan (sequenced)

### Phase 0 — toolchain proof (before any code)
Clone fork → change bundle ID → `make install` unmodified → connect to devbox.
Pairing: `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` on devbox, scan QR from the fork. Proves signing + SSH + socket transport work end-to-end. **Do not proceed to Phase 1 until this works.**

### Phase 1 — chat layer (the big one) — 2 weeks
Port Drover's transcript stack (MIT, reference: https://github.com/keinstn/drover):

**What to port** (Drover → Heeler mapping):
- `app/lib/src/transcript/native_transcript.dart` → Swift transcript models + `JsonlTranscriptWindow` (512KiB bounded tail, append-only poll, loadOlder paging). **Increase the window constant** — devbox conversations run 1.2MB+, 512KiB initial window shows only recent history
- `app/lib/src/agents/pi/pi_transcript.dart` → Swift JSONL parser (omp reuses pi's record shapes; documented in Drover's `docs/agents/omp-notes.md`)
- Fetch path: `agent.list` already returns `agent_session: {kind:'path', value:'~/.omp/...jsonl'}` over the socket API (verified live) → new `Transport.readTranscriptFile(path)` via existing SFTP
- Parser output models: `TranscriptMessage / Thinking / ToolUse / ToolResult` (Drover's shape — keep it, it maps to omp's record types)

**omp JSONL record spec** (verified against live devbox session files — use these as test fixtures):
```
type:'message'  message.role ∈ user|assistant|toolResult|bashExecution
               content blocks: {type:'text'} {type:'thinking'} {type:'toolCall', id, name, arguments}
               NB: toolCall.arguments is already-decoded JSON — do NOT re-decode
toolResult:     own top-level record, paired by toolCallId (long, contains '|')
skip records:   top-level type ∉ {message} — title, title_change, custom_message, custom
               (customType: tool_execution_start, session_exit), thinking_level_change etc.
session files:  ~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slugified-cwd>/<ISO-ts>_<uuid>.jsonl
```
Fixture source: the live devbox sessions under `~/.omp/agent/sessions/` — real 1.2MB conversation to test parser + windowing + paging against. **Critical**: the parser must be tested against these real files, not synthetic fixtures (synthetic-fixture rule).

**New `ChatScreen`** replacing Console-per-agent detail — design requirements:
- Detail levels **designed in from the start**:
  - L0 (default): assistant `text` turns only. NO thinking, NO toolcall, NO diff, NO edit, NO spinner
  - L1: + toolcall names (one line each, collapsed)
  - L2: + tool results (collapsed, tap to expand), diffs
  - L3: + thinking blocks (collapsed)
  - Level switcher: persistent small control, not a modal
- Minimal chrome: status bar reduced to a thin strip (agent name + state + workspace/host badge); everything else full-bleed chat
- Live terminal section stays (Heeler's Attach) but demoted: collapsed-by-default strip at bottom, expand on tap — it covers the gap between "last jsonl record" and "screen now"
- Per-agent detail-level memory (persist per pane id)

### Phase 3 — composer input modes — 1 week
Heeler's Composer (one-shot `agent.prompt`, Blocked-state PTY insert) is the primitive. Add a tokenizer/router in front:
- `/` → slash commands: `omp` slash commands + client-local ones (`/level 2`, `/follow <agent>`)
- `#` → tag/search: `#<workspace>`, `#<status:blocked>`, `#<agent>` — filters the blended console
- `@` → mention: `@<agent>` routes the message to that pane's `agent.prompt` (cross-host: resolve agent → host → transport)
- `!` → bash: runs via `pane run` in a scratch shell (or the agent's pane with a toggle); output inline at L1 detail, streamed
- Snippets/Skills already exist — wire `#` and Skills suggestions into the same suggestion row

### Phase 5 — keyboard enhancement — days
Existing: tools keyboard (Esc/Tab/arrows/Enter), full terminal keyboard, Snippets. Add:
- Long-press chord layer (hold a key → radial menu of variants)
- Per-agent macro keys (map a key to a Snippet with args)
- Swipe on the key row = prefix key (ctrl+b) + gesture → common herdr nav

### Phase 4 — URI/file openers — 1 week
Primitives exist: SFTP `stageFile/stageImage/readSkillFile`. Add:
- URL detection in chat text + terminal → open embedded (SFSafariViewController) or external (default browser) — per-domain setting
- Markdown file path in chat → fetch over SFTP silently → internal viewer (SwiftUI + swift-markdown or similar)
- "Open in editor": SFTP download → temp local file → `UIDocumentPickerViewController`/share to external editor → watch for change → silent SFTP push back. Start with download+push; the live-sync loop is v2 if clunky
- All remote→local transfers silent (no progress dialogs under ~10MB)

### Phase 2 — sessions/hosts blending polish — days
Console already blends Hosts; each session = a Host entry. Add UX only:
- Host badge compact display (`devbox:main` style)
- Session picker in Host edit (listSessions already exists)
- Optional: auto-discover all running sessions on a host at connect → offer to add each as a Host

## What NOT to build (decided)

- **No push in the fork** — free Apple ID can't. Upstream TestFlight Heeler covers it (already installed + paired on the devbox side)
- **No transport rewrite** — Heeler's is the reason we chose this base
- **No Drover UI port** — the Flutter Material look is what we're escaping

1. Transport additions must respect the 8+1 channel budget (ADR-0011) — flag any per-poll channel churn
2. Parser changes tested against real devbox jsonls (1.2MB file), not fixtures
3. L0 default must render zero toolcall/thinking/diff/edit chrome — verify on the wA:p7 long-running agent conversation

The fork is the interactive app; upstream Heeler delivers blocked/done alerts. If that ever becomes annoying: Bark app + self-hosted bark-server on the devbox + forked notify plugin (~50 LOC change), but two-Heeler is zero-work.

Fork signing also means: **bundle ID must change** (can't be `dev.bybee.heeler`) and builds expire in 7 days → weekly rebuild ritual.

## Weekly build ritual (MacBook, USB iPhone)

```bash
cd heeler-fork
make install          # repo-provided target: builds Debug + installs to the
                      # first physical iPhone found via devicectl
```

One-time setup:
- Xcode → fork project → Signing & Capabilities → select my Personal Team → let Xcode fix the profile
- Change bundle ID from `dev.bybee.heeler` to something personal
- `make resolve` if SPM packages need fetching
- Rebuild **before day 7** (app dies mid-flight otherwise); pick a fixed weekday

Note: `make testflight` / `make publish` targets exist but are useless for us (no paid account). `make test` runs the 155-file test suite — agents should run it before every install.

## Heeler architecture (what to review against)

Codebase: 180 Swift files, 42.9k LOC app + 3.4k host plugin (Node) + 1.3k push relay (Cloudflare Workers). 155 test files. Repo: https://github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler — clone locally before starting.

Module map (LOC) — only **bold** modules get modified/added:

| Module | LOC | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Sources/Heeler/Transport/` | 7.5k | libssh2 direct-streamlocal onto `herdr.sock`; 18 socket-API methods; events channel; jump hosts. **extend only** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Console/` | 15k | pane-text Monitor UI. **the screen we replace/supplement with chat** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Terminal/` | 6.3k | libghostty renderer, Attach PTY. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Pairing/` | 1.2k | QR pairing. untouched |
| `Sources/Heeler/Notifications/` + `LiveActivities/` | 3k | E2E APNs push. untouched (fork can't push anyway) |
| `Sources/Heeler/Files/`, `Attachments/` | 0.8k | SFTP staging. **extend for file openers** |
| `Sources/Heeler/Skills/`, `Snippets/` | 1.9k | herdr skills + snippets. **hook composer modes into these** |
| **new** `Chat/` | ~2-3k (est.) | transcript models + parser + chat renderer (ported from Drover) |

Key architecture facts (from ADRs — agents must read these before touching Transport):
- **ADR-0011**: one direct-streamlocal channel per RPC (herdr Unix API = one request per connection); long-lived reserved Events channel; 8+1 channel budget under OpenSSH `MaxSessions 10`
- **ADR-0012**: herdr API reality — `pane.read` capped at 1000 lines, no offsets, no replay on `events.subscribe`; `pane.agent_status_changed` is the push signal. THIS is why Heeler has no chat: pane text was the only history source it knew. Our chat layer bypasses this via SFTP + session JSONL (below)
- **ADR-0013**: Composer delivers via single `agent.prompt` (no `wait`); when agent is Blocked, insert-without-Enter into the Attach PTY instead
- **ADR-0015/0016**: shell terminals via `tab.create` + `herdr terminal attach --takeover`; Direct Input is opt-in
- `Host` model pins one `sessionName` (blank = default session); `listSessions()` already exists → **blending = N Host entries**, zero code

## Implementation plan (sequenced)

### Phase 0 — toolchain proof (before any code)
Clone fork → change bundle ID → `make install` unmodified → connect to devbox.
Pairing: `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` on devbox, scan QR from the fork. Proves signing + SSH + socket transport work end-to-end. **Do not proceed to Phase 1 until this works.**

### Phase 1 — chat layer (the big one) — 2 weeks
Port Drover's transcript stack (MIT, reference: https://github.com/keinstn/drover):

**What to port** (Drover → Heeler mapping):
- `app/lib/src/transcript/native_transcript.dart` → Swift transcript models + `JsonlTranscriptWindow` (512KiB bounded tail, append-only poll, loadOlder paging). **Increase the window constant** — devbox conversations run 1.2MB+, 512KiB initial window shows only recent history
- `app/lib/src/agents/pi/pi_transcript.dart` → Swift JSONL parser (omp reuses pi's record shapes; documented in Drover's `docs/agents/omp-notes.md`)
- Fetch path: `agent.list` already returns `agent_session: {kind:'path', value:'~/.omp/...jsonl'}` over the socket API (verified live) → new `Transport.readTranscriptFile(path)` via existing SFTP
- Parser output models: `TranscriptMessage / Thinking / ToolUse / ToolResult` (Drover's shape — keep it, it maps to omp's record types)

**omp JSONL record spec** (verified against live devbox session files — use these as test fixtures):
```
type:'message'  message.role ∈ user|assistant|toolResult|bashExecution
               content blocks: {type:'text'} {type:'thinking'} {type:'toolCall', id, name, arguments}
               NB: toolCall.arguments is already-decoded JSON — do NOT re-decode
toolResult:     own top-level record, paired by toolCallId (long, contains '|')
skip records:   top-level type ∉ {message} — title, title_change, custom_message, custom
               (customType: tool_execution_start, session_exit), thinking_level_change etc.
session files:  ~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slugified-cwd>/<ISO-ts>_<uuid>.jsonl
```
Fixture source: the live devbox sessions under `~/.omp/agent/sessions/` — real 1.2MB conversation to test parser + windowing + paging against. **Critical**: the parser must be tested against these real files, not synthetic fixtures (synthetic-fixture rule).

**New `ChatScreen`** replacing Console-per-agent detail — design requirements:
- Detail levels **designed in from the start**:
  - L0 (default): assistant `text` turns only. NO thinking, NO toolcall, NO diff, NO edit, NO spinner
  - L1: + toolcall names (one line each, collapsed)
  - L2: + tool results (collapsed, tap to expand), diffs
  - L3: + thinking blocks (collapsed)
  - Level switcher: persistent small control, not a modal
- Minimal chrome: status bar reduced to a thin strip (agent name + state + workspace/host badge); everything else full-bleed chat
- Live terminal section stays (Heeler's Attach) but demoted: collapsed-by-default strip at bottom, expand on tap — it covers the gap between "last jsonl record" and "screen now"
- Per-agent detail-level memory (persist per pane id)

### Phase 2 — composer input modes — 1 week
Heeler's Composer (one-shot `agent.prompt`, Blocked-state PTY insert) is the primitive. Add a tokenizer/router in front:
- `/` → slash commands: `omp` slash commands + client-local ones (`/level 2`, `/follow <agent>`)
- `#` → tag/search: `#<workspace>`, `#<status:blocked>`, `#<agent>` — filters the blended console
- `@` → mention: `@<agent>` routes the message to that pane's `agent.prompt` (cross-host: resolve agent → host → transport)
- `!` → bash: runs via `pane run` in a scratch shell (or the agent's pane with a toggle); output inline at L1 detail, streamed
- Snippets/Skills already exist — wire `#` and Skills suggestions into the same suggestion row

### Phase 3 — keyboard enhancement — days
Existing: tools keyboard (Esc/Tab/arrows/Enter), full terminal keyboard, Snippets. Add:
- Long-press chord layer (hold a key → radial menu of variants)
- Per-agent macro keys (map a key to a Snippet with args)
- Swipe on the key row = prefix key (ctrl+b) + gesture → common herdr nav

### Phase 4 — URI/file openers — 1 week
Primitives exist: SFTP `stageFile/stageImage/readSkillFile`. Add:
- URL detection in chat text + terminal → open embedded (SFSafariViewController) or external (default browser) — per-domain setting
- Markdown file path in chat → fetch over SFTP silently → internal viewer (SwiftUI + swift-markdown or similar)
- "Open in editor": SFTP download → temp local file → `UIDocumentPickerViewController`/share to external editor → watch for change → silent SFTP push back. Start with download+push; the live-sync loop is v2 if clunky
- All remote→local transfers silent (no progress dialogs under ~10MB)

### Phase 5 — sessions/hosts blending polish — days
Console already blends Hosts; each session = a Host entry. Add UX only:
- Host badge compact display (`devbox:main` style)
- Session picker in Host edit (listSessions already exists)
- Optional: auto-discover all running sessions on a host at connect → offer to add each as a Host

## What NOT to build (decided)

- **No push in the fork** — free Apple ID can't. Upstream TestFlight Heeler covers it (already installed + paired on the devbox side)
- **No transport rewrite** — Heeler's is the reason we chose this base
- **No Drover UI port** — the Flutter Material look is what we're escaping
- **No Firebase anything** — Drover's path only; we keep zero Google in the loop

## Review checklist (for me, when agents bring code)

1. Transport additions must respect the 8+1 channel budget (ADR-0011) — flag any per-poll channel churn
2. Parser changes tested against real devbox jsonls (1.2MB file), not fixtures
3. L0 default must render zero toolcall/thinking/diff/edit chrome — verify on the wA:p7 long-running agent conversation
4. New modules only (Chat/, composer router) — anything touching Transport/ or Terminal/ gets extra scrutiny
5. `make test` green before every weekly install
6. Upstream merges: rebase weekly from ZingerLittleBee/Heeler main — our changes are layered, merges should be near-free; if a merge touches Chat/, re-read their ADR diff first
7. License: keep NOTICE + Apache-2.0 headers; ported Drover parser code carries MIT attribution comment

## Open questions (resolve during Phase 0/1)

- [ ] dartssh2-style streamlocal in the fork is irrelevant (Heeler uses libssh2 already) — but verify the fork builds with the pinned XCFrameworks without paid account (they're checked in, should be fine)
- [ ] Decide L0 for *blocked* agents: does a pending `ask`/permission prompt force L2 detail for that turn? (probably yes — prompt visibility beats minimalism)
- [ ] omp `ask` tool dialogs are arrow-key, not numbered — the chat layer should render pending `ask` as tappable options (Drover hasn't done this; it's our chance to beat upstream on it)
- [ ] Should `!` bash mode get its own scratch pane or reuse the agent's pane? (scratch pane safer; agent pane faster to reach)

## Reference material

- Heeler repo + ADRs: https://github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler (`docs/adr/`, `CONTEXT.md`, `plugin/README.md`)
- Drover parser reference: https://github.com/keinstn/drover (`app/lib/src/transcript/`, `app/lib/src/agents/pi/`, `docs/agents/omp-notes.md` — the omp record spec)
- Drover upstream may evolve the parser (ships weekly) — pin a commit when porting, note it here
- Heeler TestFlight (notification surface): https://testflight.apple.com/join/aXSxRn4r
- herdr docs: https://herdr.dev/llms.txt — socket API + integrations
- Live fixtures on devbox: `~/.omp/agent/sessions/*/` (real omp jsonls); `herdr api snapshot --json` shapes

## Devbox host-side state (already done, for reference)

- herdr 0.9.0, default session is THE session (all agents migrated there 2026-09-13)
- omp integration installed: `herdr integration install omp` → `~/.omp/agent/extensions/herdr-omp-agent-state.ts` — **only fires at agent start**; agents started before install have no `agent_session` (bounce to register: ctrl+c + `omp --resume <jsonl>`)
- Heeler plugin installed + paired candidate: `herdr plugin list` shows heeler v0.4.0; pairing QR via `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` (2-min single-use window — invoke on demand)
- Drover also installed on the phone (PEM key auth, `~/.ssh/drover_devbox` entry in authorized_keys) — coexists; its omp chat works today

# TIL Session Harvest

Persist only what makes future sessions better. Compact operational updates, not
transcript summaries.

Never commit, push, amend, or force-push unless explicitly asked. (`chezmoi
add`/`re-add` is the expected sync and does not count — chezmoi autoCommits.)

## 1. Gather

Default to the visible conversation. If you need more, the session tools are
`session_read(from_end=true, limit=N)` (sessions are large; durable signal
clusters near the end), plus `session_search` / `session_list` / `session_info`.
Search for `remember`, `gotcha`, `root cause`, `workaround`, `always`, `never`,
`follow-up`, `fixed`, `lesson`, `do not`, plus project terms. Also usable: files
changed this session, user handoff notes. Ask only if picking the wrong session
would cause misleading or destructive updates.

## 2. Filter

Persist a candidate only if **verified**, **safe**, **not already captured**, and
it does at least one of:

- Prevents repeating a costly mistake.
- Documents a non-obvious workflow or command sequence.
- Captures a stable architectural decision, invariant, or ownership boundary.
- Records a recurring tool/environment gotcha.
- Defines a reusable triage/debug/deploy procedure.
- Clarifies path, naming, memory, skill, repo-doc, or chezmoi conventions.
- Corrects a misconception future agents may otherwise repeat.

Drop: one-off status and transient IDs; facts easily rediscovered from code;
unverified speculation; raw logs (distill to symptom / root cause / fix);
anything already recorded elsewhere. Omit disproven hypotheses, or mark them
retracted.

**Never store** passwords, API keys, OAuth tokens, cookies, private keys, bearer
tokens, credential files, secret env values, or unconsented personal data.
Credential *names* and encrypted storage locations are fine. If unsure, skip and
list under "Proposed, not applied" — as with anything ambiguous or low-confidence.

## 3. Route

First match wins:

1. **Compact fact, invariant, preference, or path convention** -> memory.
2. **Repeatable workflow, tool usage, or decision rules** -> skill.
3. **Fits both** -> route by access pattern: always-relevant and needed even when
   no trigger fires -> memory; invoked deliberately -> skill. If it is genuinely
   both a fact AND a procedure, split them — compact fact in memory pointing at
   the skill that holds the procedure. Never duplicate the procedure into memory.
4. **Team-facing project knowledge** -> tracked repo doc.
5. **Current-session status only** -> leave it in the report.

Then read only the reference for the surface you chose:

|Surface|Read|
|---|---|
|Memory — procedure, scope, overflow-means-relocate, and the **mandatory chezmoi sync step**|[references/persist-to-memory.md](references/persist-to-memory.md)|
|Skill — checklist, keeping SKILL.md lean, discoverability, `add` vs `re-add` vs template traps|[references/persist-to-skill.md](references/persist-to-skill.md)|
|Repo doc — placement, and why `.agents/`/`.opencode/` are wrong for team knowledge but right for personal project skills|[references/persist-to-repo-doc.md](references/persist-to-repo-doc.md)|

## 4. Verify, then report

Confirm before reporting: everything edited is synced (`chezmoi status` clean for
touched paths; global memory needs an explicit `re-add`), and no literal
`\u2014`-style escapes were written into any file.

Include only sections that have content — omit empty ones rather than writing
"None".

```markdown
## TIL harvest complete

### Applied
- Memory: `<scope>/<label>` — <summary>
- Skill: `<name>` — <created/updated and why>
- Repo doc: `<path>` — <created/updated and why>

### Proposed, not applied
- <candidate> — <reason>

### Skipped
- <category> — <reason>

### Safety notes
- Secrets stored: none

### Follow-ups
- <action the user still needs to take>
```

## Cross-references

- `memory-harvest` — the maintenance sweep over memory that ALREADY exists.
- `chezmoi-authoring` — authoritative sync mechanics; defer, don't re-derive.
- `repo-root-agent-docs` (global memory) — "memory overflow = wrong surface".

---

Resolve relative paths in this skill (e.g. `scripts/foo.js`, `templates/config.yaml`) against this absolute directory; read referenced assets and templates; run scripts with the terminal tool when skill instructions call for it.

displayContent.text:
# Persisting to a skill

A skill is the **trigger-gated** surface: it costs nothing until its description
matches, then the loader reads the WHOLE `SKILL.md`. Use it for procedural
knowledge, tool sequences, and decision rules invoked deliberately.

Skills were the destination in ~51% of past TIL harvests. Prefer ADDING to an
existing themed skill over spawning a new one.

## Where skills live

| Kind | Live path | Syncs? |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Global personal skill | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | yes, chezmoi-tracked |
| Project skill (personal, repo-local) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | no, git-ignored |

Always write or edit the **live** path first. In user-facing reports, name the
live path; mention the chezmoi source path only as a parenthetical.

A project skill is for *your own* local behavior in one repo. It is git-ignored,
so it is invisible to teammates and does not sync across machines. If the
knowledge is team-facing, it belongs in a tracked repo doc instead — see
[persist-to-repo-doc.md](persist-to-repo-doc.md).

## Checklist for a new or edited skill

- Short kebab-case name.
- Strong YAML `description` with concrete triggers a future session would say.
- Explicit scope AND exclusions ("Does NOT cover ..." pointing at the sibling
  skill that does).
- Concise workflow and decision rules; no transcripts.
- Safety rules for tools, secrets, and destructive operations.
- Cross-references instead of duplicated bodies.

## Keep SKILL.md lean

The loader reads the whole file on every trigger, so inline bulk taxes every
load.

- **Runnable scripts** -> `~/.agents/skills/<name>/scripts/<file>`, replaced in
  the body by a short table of links (`[scripts/foo.sh](scripts/foo.sh)`).
  Precedent: `asset-harvest-pipeline`.
- **Long topical prose** -> `~/.agents/skills/<name>/references/<topic>.md`, with
  a "When to read which reference" table in `SKILL.md` and an instruction to read
  only the relevant one. Precedent: `scenario-studio-backend`.

Keep a naturally-sequential pipeline as ONE skill. Do not shatter a continuous
workflow into fragments that only cross-reference each other.

## Discoverability when a skill holds a sub-topic its NAME hides

A name-scan of `ls ~/.agents/skills/` will not reveal buried knowledge, and body
text only helps semantic matching. So:

1. Name the sub-topic explicitly in the `description`, with its own triggers.
2. Add a cross-reference from the SIBLING skill someone would wrongly check
   first (e.g. point at `scenario-studio-nre-fixture` from
   `scenario-studio-backend`'s "Does NOT cover" line).

Prefer widening triggers plus cross-references over renaming — a rename breaks
the chezmoi source path.

## Syncing a skill (get the verb right)

| Situation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| **New** file chezmoi has never seen | `chezmoi add <live-path>` |
| **Existing** tracked plain file you edited | `chezmoi re-add <live-path>` |
| Target is template-backed (`.tmpl`) or a symlink | **neither** — edit the SOURCE directly |

Traps, all confirmed:

- `chezmoi re-add` is a **silent no-op with exit 0** on a template-backed target.
  The source keeps the old content and the next `chezmoi apply` REVERTS your live
  file. Check first: `chezmoi source-path <live-path>` — if it ends `.tmpl` or
  starts `symlink_`, edit the source directly. (`symlink_omarchy` is such a case.)
- Never `chezmoi add --recursive ~/.agents/skills` — it hits an interactive
  "would remove template attribute" prompt on templated/symlinked siblings and
  hangs with no TTY. Add new files **individually**.
- A chained `chezmoi re-add A B` aborts on the first unmanaged path and silently
  skips the rest. One path at a time, or `chezmoi add` the orphan first.
- chezmoi stores an executable as `executable_<name>`; if the name also begins
  with a chezmoi keyword (`run_`, `dot_`) it becomes `executable_literal_<name>`.
  Expected, not a bug.

Verify after syncing:

```bash
chezmoi status ~/.agents/skills/<name>     # empty output == clean
chezmoi diff   ~/.agents/skills/<name>     # empty == live equals source
```

`autoCommit` + `autoPush` are on, so a successful add/re-add commits and pushes.

After a live `py_compile` or import test, delete any stray `scripts/__pycache__`
before finishing, and confirm it did not get chezmoi-added.

Full chezmoi mechanics live in the `chezmoi-authoring` skill — defer to it rather
than re-deriving them here.

## Writing gotcha: no escaped unicode

Write real characters. A literal `\u2014` or `\u2192` surviving into the file is
a bug from a JSON-quoted tool argument. Grep the file after writing.

# Persisting to memory

Memory is the **always-in-context** surface: every block loads on every turn, in
every session, whether or not a trigger fires. That is its value and its cost.
Use it only for compact facts the agent must have *without knowing to ask*.

Memory was the destination in ~69% of past TIL harvests — it is the default, but
the default is easy to overfill. Read the overflow rule below before appending.

## Procedure

1. Call `memory_list(scope="all")` before creating or updating anything.
2. Prefer updating the best existing block over creating a near-duplicate.
   Two overlapping blocks are a permanent maintenance hazard: collapse the weaker
   one into a pointer at the stronger one.
3. `memory_replace` for surgical edits. `memory_set` only for a new block or a
   deliberate full rewrite.
4. Check the char limit (~5000) *before* writing. If the block is near-full, do
   not append — see the overflow rule.
5. Keep entries operational: rules, commands, paths, symptoms, root causes,
   fixes, decisions. Not narrative.
6. **Sync it** — see the sync step below. This is not optional.

## Scope

- `global` — cross-project user, tooling, or OpenCode facts.
  Lives at `~/.agents/memory/*.md` (canonical; `~/.config/opencode/memory` —
  the opencode plugin's hardcoded path — and `~/.agents/rules`, the omp rules
  mount, are symlinks into it). **chezmoi-tracked, syncs.**
- `project` — repo-specific architecture, commands, workflows, gotchas.
  Lives at `<repo>/.agents/memory/*.md` (canonical; `<repo>/.opencode/memory`
  and `<repo>/.agents/rules` are symlinks into it). **git-ignored,
  local-only, does NOT sync.** Anything durable that lives only here is
  lost on another machine.

`memory_set` / `memory_replace` only target the CURRENT cwd's project scope. A
block belonging to another repo's cwd must be edited as an on-disk file.

## Overflow is a SIGNAL to relocate, not to cram

When a block approaches or hits its ~5000-char limit, that means the content is
too long or too detailed **for memory**, not that you should compress harder.

Do NOT keep force-fitting detail into a near-full block. That risks overflow and
keeps low-value detail always-in-context on every turn forever.

Instead:

- Procedural / trigger-gated body -> move to a **skill**.
- Team-facing project state / long-form record -> move to a **tracked repo doc**.
- Leave only a **compact pointer** in the memory block.

Established precedents to copy: the `opencode-setup` memory -> skill pattern and
the `second-disk-btrfs-migration` memory -> skill pattern. The rule also lives in
the `repo-root-agent-docs` global block under "Memory-block overflow = wrong
surface".

If relocating would take more than a trivial edit, list it under "Proposed, not
applied" rather than silently truncating something already in the block.

## Sync step (MANDATORY for `global` blocks)

Global memory is chezmoi-tracked but **not auto-captured**. OpenCode rewrites
these files live; chezmoi only learns about it when you re-add:

```bash
chezmoi re-add ~/.agents/memory/                   # EXISTING blocks you edited
chezmoi add ~/.agents/memory/<new>.md              # each NEWLY CREATED block
chezmoi status ~/.agents/memory                    # empty output == clean
`autoCommit` + `autoPush` are enabled, so both commit and push themselves.

### `re-add` SILENTLY SKIPS files chezmoi does not already track

`re-add` only refreshes **tracked** files. A memory block created this session is
untracked, so `re-add` ignores it — and `chezmoi status` then reports **clean**,
because chezmoi does not know the file exists. Clean status is therefore NOT
proof of sync for a new block.

Verified 2026-08-11: two new blocks passed `re-add` + a clean `status`, yet both
were absent from the remote. Only a direct remote check caught it.

Always verify against the REMOTE, not against status:

```bash
cd ~/.local/share/chezmoi && git fetch origin main
git rev-parse HEAD; git rev-parse origin/main            # must match
git show origin/main:dot_agents/memory/<label>.md | wc -l        # must be > 0

Direction is always **live -> source** (`add`/`re-add`). Never `chezmoi apply`
onto a box whose live memory is newer — that overwrites fresh session learnings
with an older source copy.

`project` blocks are git-ignored and local-only: no sync step, nothing to do.

## Good memory shape

```markdown
# <topic>

## Rule
<the durable rule>

## Procedure
1. ...

## Gotchas
- ...
```

## Writing gotcha: no escaped unicode

Write real characters directly. If content is routed through a JSON-quoted tool
argument, decode it before it lands in the file — a literal `\u2014` or `\u2192`
in the text is a bug, not an em-dash. Grep the file after writing.

  session", "migrate agents between herdr sessions", "consolidate to one
  session", "agent not detected after migration", "agent_session missing",
  "bounce an agent to register the integration", "omp chat history missing in

# herdr session migration (verified 2026-09-13, herdr 0.9.0)

## Why a procedure: herdr sessions are separate servers

Each session is an independent server with its own socket
(`~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock` vs `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<name>/herdr.sock`).
`herdr pane move` works ONLY within one session. Cross-session "move" =
recreate the pane in the target session and resume the agent's session file
there. Agent conversation state lives in the agent CLI's own session file
(e.g. omp: `~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slug-cwd>/<ISO-ts>_<uuid>.jsonl`), NOT in
herdr — so resume is lossless for idle agents.

## Migration recipe (per agent)

```bash
# 1. Collect from source session: pane, cwd, jsonl path, title
herdr --session <src> agent list | python3 -m json.tool   # agent_session.value = jsonl

# 2. Create tab in target session at the agent's cwd
herdr --session <dst> tab create --cwd <cwd> --label "<title>"
#   (optionally --workspace <id>)

# 3. Resume the agent in the new pane
herdr --session <dst> pane run <new-pane> "omp --resume <jsonl>"

# 4. VERIFY agent detected in target (status + title), then close old pane
herdr --session <dst> agent list
herdr --session <src> pane close <old-pane>
```

## Traps (all hit live)

- **Pane IDs shift when tabs/panes move or close.** An ID read minutes ago can
  now name a different pane — moving `w6:p4` by stale ID once relocated a stale
  SHELL, not the agent. Re-derive IDs from `agent list` immediately before
  EVERY move; verify pane→agent mapping from `agent list` (pane_id +
  terminal_title_stripped), never from memory.
- **Tab labels are unrecoverable.** Capture old tab labels BEFORE closing the
  source panes (herdr keeps them nowhere accessible); new tabs get `--label`
  from you.
- **Never migrate a `working` agent** — the in-flight turn's un-flushed output
  is lost on pane close. Wait for `idle` (e.g. `herdr --session <src> agent
  wait <pane> --state idle`). Exception: if its session file has not been
  written for >10 min, the turn is stalled; resume-alongside is safe.
- **Two omp processes on one jsonl corrupt it.** Create the resumed instance,
  verify history loaded, THEN close the old pane — never leave both running.
- `pane read <pane> --lines N` shows the pane tail: use it to confirm the
  resumed TUI drew the right conversation before killing the original.

## Re-registering agents after installing a herdr integration

`herdr integration install omp` (or pi/claude/codex/copilot) writes the agent
CLI hook (`~/.omp/agent/extensions/herdr-omp-agent-state.ts`), but it fires
**only at agent process start**. Agents already running have NO
`agent_session` registered → transcript-parsing clients (Drover, any chat
renderer) silently fall back to pane-text. Fix = bounce each agent in place:

```bash
herdr --session <s> pane send-text <pane> $'\x03\x03'   # ctrl+c, back to shell
sleep 1
herdr --session <s> pane run <pane> "omp --resume <jsonl>"
# verify agent list shows agent_session.value again
```

## Session consolidation facts

- Bare `herdr` always attaches the `default` session — it cannot be deleted
  conceptually. Mobile clients without a session picker (Drover) land there,
  so "one session" means moving everything INTO default.
- `herdr --session <name> server stop` stops that session's server + panes;
  `herdr session delete <name>` then removes it (default cannot be deleted).
- Sessions that only LOOK dead may hold the one running agent you want —
  check `herdr --session <name> agent list` before `server stop`.

# herdr on this box — quick refs

herdr = terminal workspace manager for AI coding agents (tmux analog:
workspace/tab/pane ≈ tmux session/window/pane). Installed via mise
(`~/.local/share/mise/installs/herdr/`). User's prefix: `f12` opens the
which-key popup (plugin), native prefix is `ctrl+f12`.

## Paths

- Config: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi-tracked since 2026-09-11
  (plain file, no template). So is the whichkey keymap
  `~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/houz42.whichkey/keys.json`. Everything else
  under ~/.config/herdr (session.json, logs, sessions/) stays untracked.
- Other machines provision the whichkey plugin via chezmoi hook
  `run_onchange_after_herdr-plugins.sh.tmpl` (idempotent `herdr plugin
  install ... --yes`, skips when herdr or the plugin is absent/present).
- Session sockets: `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<name>/herdr.sock` (NDJSON JSON
  RPC; `{"id","method","params"}` per line).
- Plugin config/state: `~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/<id>/`,
  `~/.local/state/herdr/plugins/<id>/`.
- Logs: `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log` (stale-prone; prefer
  `herdr plugin log list` / plugin state-dir logs for debugging).

## Sessions (2026-09-14 state)

- `default` is THE session (all agents consolidated there 2026-09-13);
  bare `herdr` always attaches it. `main` holds only the current
  conversation pane, will be stopped+deleted once it's done.
- Bare `herdr` cannot target a non-default session — mobile clients
  without a session picker land in `default`; moving agents BETWEEN
  sessions = resume-and-recreate (see herdr-session-migration skill).
- omp integration installed (`~/.omp/agent/extensions/`)
  — registers `agent_session` ONLY at agent start; bounce agents
  (ctrl+c + `omp --resume <jsonl>`) to register pre-existing ones.
- heeler plugin v0.4.0 installed (pairing + E2E push hooks);
  pair via `herdr plugin action invoke heeler.pair` (2-min single-use QR).
- Drover iOS client on phone: PEM key at `~/.ssh/drover_devbox` (pub in
  authorized_keys); remove the private key file once phone copy confirmed.

## Ops

- Docs index: https://herdr.dev/llms.txt (raw per-tag sources);
  `herdr api schema --json` = full socket API schema. CLI help hides
  `herdr plugin` — it exists.
- `herdr server reload-config` reports config diagnostics; always check them
  after editing config.toml (it caught a [[keys.command]] TOML misplacement
  that silently ate 20+ bindings).
- Self-test any pane UI headlessly: `herdr pane send-keys`/`send-text`/
  `read` — see herdr-plugin-dev skill.
- Agent CLI sessions (omp) live OUTSIDE herdr:
  `~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slug-cwd>/<ts>_<uuid>.jsonl` — the conversation
  truth; `herdr agent list` reports each pane's via `agent_session.value`.

## Skills

- `herdr-plugin-dev` — authoring/testing/publishing herdr plugins, popup
  API limits (no anchor, modal-only, no prefix events).
- `herdr-remote-machines` — SSH machines, `--remote` attach, multi-machine.
- `herdr-session-migration` — moving agents between herdr sessions
  (resume-and-recreate), re-registering agents after integration install,
  pane-ID-shift and tab-label traps.

## Own plugins

- `houz42.whichkey` (~/dev/herdr-whichkey, github.com/houz42/herdr-whichkey):
  which-key popup on f12, dispatches via CLI. Key tree:
  `herdr plugin config-dir houz42.whichkey` → keys.json.

# herdr iOS clients — survey facts (2026-09-14, for the Heeler fork project)

Build plan (with full implementation sequence) lives in the Obsidian vault:
`2-Notes/Heeler fork - iOS herdr client build plan.md` — do not re-research;
read that first.

## Decision

Fork **Heeler** (Apache-2.0, SwiftUI, github.com/ZingerLittleBee/Heeler) and
port Drover's omp transcript parser into it. NOT Drover as base (its transport
is herdr-CLI-over-SSH-exec, rejected) and NOT Whip (AGPL + no installable iOS
build — iOS is compile-validation only, CI ships unsigned artifacts).
Drover (keinstn/drover, MIT) = parser reference only
(`app/lib/src/transcript/native_transcript.dart`, `agents/pi/pi_transcript.dart`,
`docs/agents/omp-notes.md` = omp JSONL record spec).

## Client landscape (open-source-free only)

- **Heeler**: socket API over libssh2 direct-streamlocal onto herdr.sock
  (ADR-0011, 8+1 channel budget under MaxSessions 10); events channel;
  `agent.list/prompt/read/start/rename/send_keys`, workspace/tab/worktree
  methods; libghostty terminal; QR pairing (single-use 2-min bootstrap key,
  self-revoking); E2E AES-256-GCM APNs push via stateless Cloudflare-Workers
  relay (relay sees ciphertext only; custom relay URL possible in self-built
  apps). 155 test files; ADR paper trail; built agent-driven
  (`.testloop/reports/`). App Store + TestFlight (NOT in China store — use
  TestFlight https://testflight.apple.com/join/aXSxRn4r).
- **Drover**: dartssh2 + `herdr` CLI per exec; native omp/pi/claude/codex/
  copilot chat via SFTP-read JSONL (512KiB bounded tail window + append-poll
  + loadOlder); permission prompts→buttons (omp `ask` is arrow-key, NOT
  detected — known gap); push = Firebase Functions (plaintext event metadata
  to Google, NOT E2E); on-device speech; 4★ solo dev, ships weekly.
- **Whip**: Rust core + React Native; strongest engineering (russh, binary
  frames, no JSON over RN boundary) but AGPL and iOS-unbuildable in practice.
- **Multiplex**: Apache-2.0, visionOS-first, Pro IAP ($19.99) gates features.
- Closed-source excluded: Moshi (subscription), ShadowTerm ($29.99).

## Hard constraints (Apple, verified)

- Free Apple ID: personal-team signing = **no `aps-environment` entitlement**
  — a self-built fork can NEVER do APNs push regardless of base. Weekly
  7-day expiry; ≤3 personal apps; no TestFlight.
- Therefore the fork's notification surface = upstream Heeler TestFlight kept
  installed on the phone (its plugin already installed on devbox; two binaries
  + two Device Keys coexist fine). Fallback: Bark app + self-hosted
  bark-server on devbox (~50 LOC plugin change).
- Heeler fork build ritual on the MacBook: `make install` (repo target,
  devicectl auto-finds USB iPhone). Bundle ID must change from
  `dev.bybee.heeler`.

## omp JSONL records (verified against live devbox files)

`type:'message'` w/ role user|assistant|toolResult|bashExecution; content
blocks text/thinking/toolCall (arguments ALREADY decoded JSON — do not
re-decode); toolResult = own top-level record paired by toolCallId (long,
contains '|'); SKIP non-message top-level types (title, title_change,
custom_message, custom: tool_execution_start/session_exit). Session files:
`~/.omp/agent/sessions/<slug-cwd>/<ISO-ts>_<uuid>.jsonl`. Real 1.2MB fixture:
`~/.omp/agent/sessions/-.config-herdr/2026-09-13T09-33-26*.jsonl`.
Drover renders chat + "Live terminal" section BY DESIGN (pane tail shown when
not duplicating chat tail) — mixed chat+terminal view is intended, not a bug.

  `agent.list/prompt/read/start/rename/send_keys`, workspace/tab/worktree
  methods; libghostty terminal; QR pairing (single-use 2-min bootstrap key,
  self-revoking); E2E AES-256-GCM APNs push via stateless Cloudflare-Workers
  relay (relay sees ciphertext only; custom relay URL possible in self-built
  apps). 155 test files; ADR paper trail; built agent-driven
  (`.testloop/reports/`). App Store + TestFlight (NOT in China store — use
  TestFlight https://testflight.apple.com/join/aXSxRn4r).
- **Drover**: dartssh2 + `herdr` CLI per exec; native omp/pi/claude/codex/
  copilot chat via SFTP-read JSONL (512KiB bounded tail window + append-poll
  + loadOlder); permission prompts→buttons (omp `ask` is arrow-key, NOT
  detected — known gap); push = Firebase Functions (plaintext event metadata
  to Google, NOT E2E); on-device speech; 4★ solo dev, ships weekly.
- **Whip**: Rust core + React Native; strongest engineering (russh, binary
  frames, no JSON over RN boundary) but AGPL and iOS-unbuildable in practice.
- **Multiplex**: Apache-2.0, visionOS-first, Pro IAP ($19.99) gates features.
- Closed-source excluded: Moshi (subscription), ShadowTerm ($29.99).

## Hard constraints (Apple, verified)

- Free Apple ID: personal-team signing = **no `aps-environment` entitlement**
  — a self-built fork can NEVER do APNs push regardless of base. Weekly
  7-day expiry; ≤3 personal apps; no TestFlight.
- Therefore the fork's notification surface = upstream Heeler TestFlight kept
  installed on the phone (its plugin already installed on devbox; two binaries
  + two Device Keys coexist fine). Fallback: Bark app + self-hosted
  bark-server on devbox (~50 LOC plugin change).
- Heeler fork build ritual on the MacBook: `make install` (repo target,
  devicectl auto-finds USB iPhone). Bundle ID must change from
  `dev.bybee.heeler`.
